note: Detailed forms of the recorded policies. Each states the same policy as its concise form with the thresholds, safeguards and exceptions it implies, so that the detailed version of a case has detailed policies. Keyed by case id and policy id. Policies without an entry fall back to their concise text.

policies.M001:c01: Proceed when the refusal is documented after counselling and a patient-specific bloodless plan keeps residual operative risk within the range the team can defend. The plan names the conservation measures to be used, the point at which the operation would be abandoned, and who decides intraoperatively; if it cannot meet that range, the operation does not proceed under this policy.
policies.M001:c02: Proceed only with enhanced safeguards in place: an experienced bloodless team or centre, product-by-product preferences recorded in writing, an agreed blood-conservation protocol, contingency planning for major bleeding, and a documented shared understanding of residual mortality risk. A safeguard that cannot be met is a reason to defer rather than to proceed with a weaker version of it.
policies.M001:c03: Modify, postpone or decline the elective procedure when the unavailability of transfusion puts residual risk above the threshold the clinician or institution can defend, stating that threshold and the estimate it was applied to. Declining carries a duty to offer modification, alternative timing or referral to a centre that can meet the plan, arranged rather than suggested.
policies.M001:c04: Treat the competent patient's informed refusal as controlling, and do not make willingness to receive blood an independent condition of access where the operation is otherwise professionally acceptable. Access may still turn on ordinary clinical criteria, but any decision to decline must name a reason that would apply equally to a patient who accepted transfusion.
policies.M001:c05: Give the competent patient unusually broad authority to accept personal procedural risk: proceed unless the operation falls outside accepted technical standards or imposes material risk on others. Where the patient's own risk is high but the technique is standard, the patient's acceptance settles it, recorded after counselling that states the mortality estimate.
policies.M001:c06: Permit an individual clinician to decline participation on professional-integrity grounds even where another competent team would accept the bloodless plan, provided the patient is told at once, care continues until transfer, and an alternative clinician or centre is arranged rather than left to the patient to find.
policies.M001:c07: Keep the operation available at the patient's own hospital rather than transferring or postponing, so that refusing transfusion does not cost timely access others receive locally. Where the local capability is genuinely absent, the hospital arranges the transfer, manages the delay clinically, and records what was unavailable and why.
policies.M002:c01: Individualise support to the patient's expressed preferences and reassess during the best available period before transferring authority: adjust timing, setting, communication and symptom control first, and record what was tried. Authority transfers only after that support has been attempted and documented.
policies.M002:c02: Maximise the supported exercise of the person's own will and preferences throughout the decision window, using their preferred communication, chosen supporters and best time of day. Where their will cannot be directly ascertained, act on the best interpretation of it drawn from what they have said and done, rather than transferring authority to a substitute decision-maker.
policies.M002:c03: Provide reasonable support, make a capacity assessment specific to this decision rather than global, and move to an appropriate surrogate only where the relevant capacity remains absent after that support. The assessment records what was assessed, what support was given, and what the person could and could not do.
policies.M002:c04: Where the treatment window is closing and supported reassessment still shows an inability to appreciate a grave consequence, permit a protective or surrogate decision bounded to that decision, for that period, while continuing to involve the patient. The bound is stated in advance and revisited when the window changes.
policies.M002:c05: If the patient cannot presently decide, use substituted judgment anchored in their prior values and stable commitments, drawn from recorded statements, documented conversations and their own long-standing choices rather than from a single recent remark or from what those around them prefer.
policies.M002:c06: Where prior values do not resolve the choice, use a best-interests standard focused on expected benefits, burdens and the preservation of future agency, and record which of those considerations decided it so that the reasoning can be revisited when the person's situation changes.
policies.M002:c07: If it is clinically safe to do so, defer the irreversible choice and optimise communication, environment and acute symptoms before concluding that authority must transfer, setting a review point rather than an open-ended delay.
policies.M003:c01: Begin the time-critical lifesaving intervention immediately under presumed consent, while records, registries and surrogates are checked in parallel by someone other than the treating team. If reliable contrary wishes emerge at any point, care is redirected then, not at the next convenient interval.
policies.M003:c02: Reserve a short predefined interval for the checks most likely to find prior wishes — the record, an accessible directive, a surrogate already present — before any irreversible treatment step, then proceed if nothing reliable is found. The interval is fixed in advance for the presentation rather than judged case by case under pressure.
policies.M003:c03: Begin reversible stabilisation immediately, and defer the most irreversible step for the longest interval the clinical situation tolerates while preferences are sought. The deferral applies only to the irreversible step; everything reversible proceeds.
policies.M003:c04: Treat the absence of contrary evidence as sufficient authorisation for immediate emergency treatment, and do not let the search for preferences consume a clinically meaningful part of the rescue window. Searching continues alongside treatment and changes it if something is found.
policies.M003:c05: Give recovery of the patient's prior autonomous wishes priority even at a material reduction in expected rescue benefit where the proposed intervention is highly invasive or irreversible, stating the reduction accepted and the point at which it becomes too large.
policies.M003:c06: Scale the search to the case: the stronger the reason to suspect a contrary prior wish and the lower the cost of delay, the more searching is required before proceeding; otherwise treat while searching. What counts as a reason to suspect one — a document, a bracelet, a family member en route — is named in advance.
policies.M004:c01: Protect confidential access to sensitive care for adolescents who can participate meaningfully in the decision, with disclosure limited to defined safety and mandatory-reporting exceptions. Those exceptions are stated to the adolescent before care, and billing, portal and record routes are configured so that confidentiality is not lost through them.
policies.M004:c02: Preserve private clinical time with the adolescent, but allow parents broader routine access to sensitive information except where law or a defined clinical reason protects confidentiality. Which categories are protected is set in advance rather than decided visit by visit.
policies.M004:c03: Maintain confidentiality, explain its limits at the start of the visit, and actively encourage voluntary parental involvement in a developmentally appropriate way without making care conditional on it. Encouragement is recorded; refusal to involve a parent does not change what is offered.
policies.M004:c04: Give the adolescent presumptive control over disclosure for the sensitive service, on the ground that confidentiality is a condition of access, trust and developing autonomy. The presumption yields only to the stated safety exceptions, and the adolescent is told when it has.
policies.M004:c05: Give parents a presumptive informational role while the patient is a minor, subject to a strong adolescent-confidentiality exception where disclosure would threaten the adolescent's welfare, access to care, or protected agency. The exception is applied by the clinician and recorded, not left to the parent's agreement.
policies.M004:c06: Use a graduated policy: confidentiality authority increases with the adolescent's demonstrated understanding and with the sensitivity of the service, while parental access increases as safety stakes rise. The gradations are written down in advance so that two clinicians reach the same result for the same adolescent.
policies.M005:c01: Tell the patient the diagnosis and material prognosis directly, involving family to whatever extent the patient chooses, and record that choice. Family involvement is arranged at the patient's request rather than assumed from their presence.
policies.M005:c02: First elicit what the patient wants to know and who they want present, then tailor disclosure to those answers, revisiting them as the illness changes rather than treating the first answer as standing indefinitely.
policies.M005:c03: Where the patient affirmatively prefers it, route serious information through a family member or other mediator they name, recording the delegation and confirming it still holds before each major disclosure.
policies.M005:c04: Where the patient wants information but prefers it staged, disclose gradually on a schedule agreed with them, with a definite route to all the information they wish to receive rather than an open-ended deferral.
policies.M005:c05: Temporarily delay selected detail where immediate disclosure would create a narrowly evidenced and serious clinical harm, naming that harm, setting a review date, and preserving the capable patient's ultimate access and decision authority.
policies.M005:c06: Honour a family's request for non-disclosure only until the clinician has assessed what the patient wants to know; the request itself is not authority to continue concealment, and the family is told at the outset that this is how it will be handled.
policies.M005:c07: Permit family-requested concealment from a capable patient without that patient's delegation where relatives reasonably believe disclosure would undermine hope or coping, recording the belief, its basis, and the point at which concealment ends.
policies.M006:c01: Disclose the known error promptly: what happened, its known consequences, what remains uncertain, an apology, the care now being given, and a commitment to scheduled updates as the investigation continues. The updates happen on the stated dates whether or not there is new information.
policies.M006:c02: Disclose the occurrence and the established facts promptly, and defer claims about preventability, individual responsibility and long-term consequence until those are established, saying explicitly which of the three is being deferred and when it will be answered.
policies.M006:c03: Disclose the event and the fact of an investigation promptly, and withhold an apology or admission of responsibility until causation and institutional responsibility are confirmed, while stating plainly that the delay concerns responsibility rather than the facts of what happened.
policies.M006:c04: Give the fullest current causal account, including preliminary hypotheses clearly labelled as such, so that the patient can take part immediately in decisions about follow-up and accountability. Each hypothesis is revisited in writing when the investigation settles it.
policies.M006:c05: Delay substantive disclosure until the internal investigation can give an accurate consolidated account, unless information is needed sooner for the patient's care, with a stated maximum period and an interim notification that an investigation is under way.
policies.M006:c06: Separate the clinical disclosure from accountability: disclose promptly and fully, then route preventability, apology and compensation through an independent process once the facts have matured, telling the patient at the outset which route handles what.
policies.M007:c01: Allow conscientious refusal to provide the service, subject to accurate information, notice given early enough to preserve timing, and a direct referral to a willing provider that the objecting clinician arranges rather than describes.
policies.M007:c02: Allow refusal of both provision and personal referral where the clinician understands referral as complicity, on condition that the institution supplies an immediate neutral access route — a named service, contactable at once — so that no navigation burden falls on the patient.
policies.M007:c03: Permit non-facilitation provided the clinician gives accurate neutral information and the patient can obtain timely alternative care through a transparent institutional process, with timeliness defined against the clinical window rather than against convenience.
policies.M007:c04: Require the objecting clinician to provide or directly facilitate care where refusal would cause material clinical harm or where timely alternative access is unavailable, with the threshold defined in advance and assessed at the time of the request rather than afterwards.
policies.M007:c05: Treat provision of lawful standard reproductive care as an obligation of the professional role that individual conscience does not defeat in patient-facing practice, while leaving conscience its ordinary scope in choosing a field of practice.
policies.M007:c06: Give conscience strong protection, including refusal to refer, provided the institution rather than the patient carries responsibility for equivalent timely access, and provided that access is demonstrated in practice rather than asserted in policy.
policies.M007:c07: Tell the patient at first contact who will provide the service and by when, so that a clinician's objection is never left as the patient's problem to solve. The name and the date are recorded, and the institution follows up if the appointment does not happen.
policies.M008:c01: Disclose the minimum information necessary to those able to reduce the threat, once the defined probability, severity and identifiability threshold is met. The threshold is written down in advance, the disclosure is limited to what those recipients need to act, and what was said to whom is recorded.
policies.M008:c02: Pursue voluntary warning, safety planning, treatment intensification or other collaborative steps first, and breach confidentiality only where those fail or the time available does not allow them. What was attempted, and why it was insufficient, is recorded before any disclosure.
policies.M008:c03: Maintain confidentiality unless the threat is imminent or highly certain, on the ground that over-prediction and broad warning duties damage the trust and treatment that reduce risk in the first place. Uncertainty is resolved in favour of continued treatment rather than disclosure.
policies.M008:c04: Warn the identifiable person directly where that is the most effective minimum-necessary protective step, telling them what they need to protect themselves and no more, and telling the patient that the warning has been given unless doing so would itself increase the danger.
policies.M008:c05: Notify a protective authority or clinical crisis pathway rather than the person at risk, unless direct warning is necessary because no pathway can act in time. The referral names the specific concern rather than the diagnosis, and the patient is told it has been made.
policies.M008:c06: Preserve confidentiality and intensify treatment or containment while the risk remains materially uncertain, reserving disclosure for a higher evidentiary threshold that is stated in advance and reviewed at defined intervals rather than left open.
policies.M008:c07: State at the start of care exactly what would be disclosed and to whom, and hold any disclosure to that stated limit, so that people can seek help without learning the rules afterwards. The statement is given in writing and repeated when the treatment changes.
policies.M009:c01: Do not offer or provide CPR where it falls outside medically reasonable options, explain the judgment and its basis to the surrogate, and route disagreement through a fair conflict-resolution process with a second opinion. The judgment is recorded with the prognosis it rests on.
policies.M009:c02: Make a strong recommendation against CPR and use informed non-dissent: explain that a DNR order will be written unless the patient or surrogate objects, allow a stated period to object, and escalate any objection through fair process rather than treating silence as agreement.
policies.M009:c03: Continue to offer CPR while any non-zero prospect of the outcome the patient values remains, and let the informed patient or surrogate decide once burdens and prognosis have been explained in terms of what recovery would look like rather than survival alone.
policies.M009:c04: Maintain full-code status temporarily while a second opinion, ethics consultation and a structured goals-of-care conversation establish whether the disagreement is about prognosis or about values, with a stated period after which the question is decided rather than left open.
policies.M009:c05: Permit unilateral non-offer where the probability of meaningful survival is extremely low and CPR cannot reverse the underlying process, on the ground that professional integrity and non-maleficence limit what may be demanded. The threshold is institutional and stated, not set by the individual clinician at the bedside.
policies.M009:c06: Give a capable patient's prior specific request for CPR, or a surrogate's substituted judgment, presumptive priority unless CPR could not restore circulation at all. Physiological futility is the only defeater, and it is documented as such.
policies.M009:c07: Scale clinician authority to the expected benefit: as benefit approaches zero and burdens rise, authority to withhold increases; where benefit remains genuinely uncertain, the decision stays shared. The point at which authority shifts is stated in advance rather than asserted afterwards.
policies.M009:c08: Keep the surrogate's request in force until a documented conversation about what CPR would and would not achieve for this patient has taken place, and record the family's view in the chart where the team decides otherwise, so that the disagreement is visible in the record.
policies.M010:c01: Allow the patient's chosen adult family member to interpret once a qualified interpreter has been offered and declined, no conflict of interest is apparent, and the clinician has verified understanding by asking the patient to state the plan back. All three steps are recorded.
policies.M010:c02: Use a qualified medical interpreter for the material parts of consent, while the chosen family member remains present for support. The division is explained to the patient in advance so that the family member's presence is not mistaken for their exclusion.
policies.M010:c03: Require qualified interpretation throughout the high-stakes consent discussion; family may support but not replace it, including where the family member is fluent and willing, because the record must show that the words consented to were accurately conveyed.
policies.M010:c04: Permit family interpretation only after a private request made without the family member present, documented, with a qualified interpreter available and a clinician finding that the arrangement is appropriate for this decision.
policies.M010:c05: Require qualified interpretation, on the ground that informed consent and equitable language access both depend on reliable comprehension, and that the burden of arranging it falls on the service rather than on the patient's family.
policies.M010:c06: Respect the competent patient's choice of a trusted adult family interpreter, after independent screening for coercion and conflict conducted without that family member present, and after the clinician has verified understanding directly.
policies.M011:c01: Pursue individual expanded access where regulatory criteria are met, the patient understands the uncertainty, the potential benefit plausibly justifies the risk, and access will not materially interfere with trials or development. Each of those four is assessed and recorded before the request is made.
policies.M011:c02: Require independent institutional or manufacturer review before access, covering the evidence threshold, safety monitoring, the effect on supply, and a plan for reporting the outcome, with the review completed within a stated period so that the process does not become the refusal.
policies.M011:c03: Decline individual access where the evidence is too immature or the request would materially compromise a fair development programme, even where the patient has no satisfactory alternative, stating which of the two grounds applies and what would change it.
policies.M011:c04: Give strong priority to the identifiable patient's rescue interest once risk is tolerable, even where efficacy is highly uncertain and evidence generation would be cleaner without access, provided the patient is told plainly that the intervention may not work.
policies.M011:c05: Protect fair access through transparent and consistently applied eligibility and allocation criteria, rather than through publicity, wealth or clinician advocacy. The criteria are published, and departures from them are recorded and reviewed.
policies.M011:c06: Restrict use to trials except in exceptionally high-evidence or near-certain rescue circumstances, on the ground that premature individual access undermines collective knowledge and exposes vulnerable patients to false hope. What counts as exceptional is defined in advance.
policies.M011:c07: Publish the access criteria and the decision timeline at the point of request, so that a patient who asks learns where they stand within days rather than through informal escalation, and receives the decision in writing with its reason.
policies.M012:c01: Provide non-endorsement assistance — records, risk counselling and follow-up planning — where a capable patient proceeds, so that ordinary care is not withdrawn and avoidable harm is reduced. The assistance is documented as continuity of care, and the clinician's assessment of the evidence is recorded alongside it.
policies.M012:c02: Counsel clearly against the intervention and avoid any assistance that could reasonably read as referral or endorsement, while continuing ordinary care if the patient proceeds independently. What will and will not be provided is stated to the patient in advance.
policies.M012:c03: Do not refer to or certify the commercial intervention as clinically supported. Provide accurate evidence and risk counselling, release records, and give necessary continuity care, with the non-endorsement stated explicitly in any document that leaves the practice.
policies.M012:c04: Respect competent risk-taking by supporting practical harm reduction and continuity, so long as the clinician does not misrepresent the evidentiary status of the intervention in any record, letter or conversation.
policies.M012:c05: Refuse referral, certification or facilitation that would lend professional legitimacy to a treatment whose meaningful benefit is unestablished, while continuing to provide care unrelated to it and saying so clearly to the patient.
policies.M012:c06: Decline all non-essential assistance connected to the commercial intervention beyond emergency and ordinary continuing care, on the ground that even logistical help predictably functions as endorsement. The boundary is stated to the patient before they travel.
policies.M013:c01: Require explicit opt-in after disclosing the trainee's identity, level, material role in the procedure, the supervision arrangements, and that declining carries no penalty. The disclosure happens before sedation and is recorded.
policies.M013:c02: Use a teaching-hospital consent architecture with clear role disclosure and a real opt-out, without a separate signature for each supervised step. The opt-out is offered at a point where it can still be exercised and is recorded when taken.
policies.M013:c03: Permit the attending to delegate ordinary supervised components within the team after general informed consent, provided the trainee is introduced by name and level and the attending remains present and responsible for the material steps.
policies.M013:c04: Scale the specificity of consent to what the trainee will do: observation and minor tasks require notification, while invasive or substantially independent performance requires explicit authorisation for that step. Which category applies is decided before the procedure, not during it.
policies.M013:c05: Give patient authorisation priority even where refusal costs a training opportunity: educational benefit does not substitute for consent to a material intervention, and refusal is recorded without consequence for the patient's care.
policies.M013:c06: Presume supervised trainee participation in a teaching institution with a meaningful opt-out, on the ground that training competent future clinicians is a shared good, while prohibiting hidden or unsupervised participation and making the presumption visible in advance.
policies.M014:c01: Respect the capable patient's refusal after informed counselling, on the ground that pregnancy does not remove bodily decisional authority. The counselling and the refusal are recorded, and the decision is revisited only if the patient asks or the clinical situation materially changes.
policies.M014:c02: Continue strong directive counselling, offer ethics and support consultation and alternatives, and revisit the decision while time allows, without coercion and without seeking a court order. Each revisiting is at the patient's agreement rather than imposed.
policies.M014:c03: After refusal, move to the safest maternal and fetal plan the patient accepts, and keep the rest of care unchanged, so that continued attention is not conditional on compliance. The alternative plan is documented as the agreed plan rather than as a fallback.
policies.M014:c04: Treat bodily autonomy as a categorical bar to forced intervention in a capable pregnant patient, even where the expected fetal benefit is substantial, and apply the bar without exception rather than as a strong presumption that could be outweighed.
policies.M014:c05: Permit exceptional override only where the fetal benefit would be extraordinarily large, the maternal burden very small, and no less intrusive alternative exists — all three at once, established in advance and reviewed by someone outside the treating team.
policies.M014:c06: Use a shared process that invites the partner, family or other supporters in only if the patient wants them, seeking a plan everyone can accept while leaving the decision with the patient. The patient is asked privately who they want present.
policies.M014:c07: Keep the refusal in force and continue full labour care unchanged, so that declining an intervention never costs a patient the rest of the team's attention, with staffing and monitoring recorded as they would be for any other patient.
policies.M015:c01: Continue caring for the child, use evidence-based communication, revisit vaccination at each visit rather than once, and keep the medical home in place despite parental refusal. Refusal is recorded without changing what the child is offered.
policies.M015:c02: Permit dismissal or non-enrolment after repeated counselling where less restrictive strategies have failed, subject to written notice with a stated period, a review of what it would cost this family to find another practice, and care continuing until the transfer is complete.
policies.M015:c03: Continue care while using infection-control and scheduling precautions for unvaccinated patients, and apply tighter restrictions during a local outbreak. The precautions are set by the practice in advance and applied uniformly rather than negotiated per family.
policies.M015:c04: Make routine vaccination a condition of continuing elective enrolment, except for recognised medical contraindications, on the ground that a practice may set collective-risk boundaries. The condition is stated at enrolment rather than introduced after a refusal.
policies.M015:c05: Preserve care because the child has an interest in a trusted medical home that is independent of the parents' decision, and should not carry the cost of it. Dismissal is not available under this policy even after repeated refusal.
policies.M015:c06: Permit dismissal on the ground that the practice also owes duties to other vulnerable patients, to staff, and to the integrity of a preventive standard, subject to notice, an alternative identified before discharge, and continuing care in the interim.
policies.M015:c07: Keep the child in the practice and place scheduling and infection-control precautions on the practice rather than the family, so that refusal does not cost the child a regular clinician. Where precautions restrict appointment times, the practice absorbs the inconvenience.
policies.M016:c01: Use intensive communication, support, second opinions and a short negotiation period that stays within the clinically safe window, before any coercive step. The window is defined by the oncology team in advance and its expiry is recorded.
policies.M016:c02: Petition child-protection or court authority where refusal crosses a serious-harm threshold and the treatment offers a high likelihood of major benefit, and only after less intrusive efforts have been tried and documented. The petition states the prognosis with and without treatment.
policies.M016:c03: Set an explicit deadline tied to the point at which further delay materially lowers the chance of cure, tell the family that date at the outset, and initiate protective intervention if refusal persists past it.
policies.M016:c04: Respect parental authority unless refusal creates imminent or near-certain catastrophic harm, on the ground that treatment burden and family integrity justify a very high threshold for state intervention. The threshold is applied to this child's prognosis rather than to the diagnosis in general.
policies.M016:c05: Treat the child's basic interests and future autonomy as overriding parental refusal where a burdensome but established therapy offers a very high chance of cure, with the chance stated numerically and confirmed by a second opinion.
policies.M016:c06: Require independent paediatric oncology and ethics review before any state action, confirming the prognosis, the benefit and burden estimates, the alternatives considered, and that mistrust or a remediable practical barrier is not what is driving the refusal.
policies.M016:c07: Offer a named second opinion and an independent family advocate before any child-protection step, so that a family that disagrees is heard rather than only reported. Both are arranged by the hospital and available within the negotiation window.
policies.M017:c01: Permit immediate reserve-agent use where the patient's expected benefit meaningfully exceeds the alternative and the case fits defined reserve criteria, with the comparison recorded at the time rather than reconstructed later.
policies.M017:c02: Require infectious-disease or stewardship preauthorisation before reserve use, with a review turnaround short enough that stewardship does not become a clinically harmful delay, and an override available where the delay itself would cause harm.
policies.M017:c03: Use the non-reserve alternative unless susceptibility, toxicity or expected-outcome differences cross a threshold defined in advance for this drug and this infection, with the crossing documented.
policies.M017:c04: Prioritise the identifiable present patient's expected benefit where the reserve drug is meaningfully better, on the ground that diffuse future resistance costs should not fall disproportionately on the patient in front of the team. Meaningfully better is defined against stated outcome differences.
policies.M017:c05: Restrict reserve use more strongly, on the ground that preserving effectiveness protects many future patients and that one patient's modest incremental benefit does not automatically outweigh that. What counts as modest is set in the authorisation rule rather than at the bedside.
policies.M017:c06: Use a written authorisation rule that weighs individual benefit, the adequacy of alternatives, the resistance-risk category of the drug, and the grounds for exception and appeal, applied consistently rather than through bedside discretion alone.
policies.M017:c07: Tell the patient when a stewardship rule rather than their own clinical picture is the reason a drug is withheld, and give them a named route to ask for that decision to be reviewed within a stated time.
policies.M018:c01: Prescribe antibiotics now, after explaining the expected benefit and the harms under this degree of diagnostic uncertainty and recording the patient's preference. The prescription is for a defined course with a review point rather than an open supply.
policies.M018:c02: Issue a back-up prescription to be filled only if named criteria are met — symptoms persisting past a stated day, a fever above a stated point, or specified new features — with those criteria written on the prescription.
policies.M018:c03: Give no antibiotic now, provide symptomatic care, and set explicit return precautions naming what should prompt reassessment and by when, with an appointment route that does not depend on the patient starting again.
policies.M018:c04: Use the delayed-prescription strategy as the default for this presentation, so that the patient holds the prescription and the criteria decide whether it is used, rather than the decision being remade at a second visit.
policies.M018:c05: Give no immediate antibiotic, on the ground that the low expected benefit does not justify the individual harms of the drug or the collective cost of resistance, with the reasoning explained to the patient and a review offered if symptoms change.
policies.M018:c06: Use a delayed prescription as an option-preserving decision made with the patient under uncertainty: the patient decides whether the criteria have been met, having been told what they are and what to do if they are not sure.
policies.M019:c01: Allow a same-day video-first assessment where no emergency red flag is present, with escalation instructions given in writing and a named route to in-person care, so that reduced travel and delay do not become reduced access to examination.
policies.M019:c02: Require in-person assessment for a new injury where hands-on findings cannot be assessed reliably by video and the patient prioritises diagnostic certainty, with the appointment arranged at the time rather than left to the patient to book.
policies.M019:c03: Start remotely only where triage shows video can support a safe initial plan, and require timely in-person assessment whenever a missing finding could materially change management. What counts as such a finding is listed for the presentation in advance.
policies.M019:c04: Prefer remote-first care for low-risk presentations, on the ground that travel and time burdens are ethically material, and escalate where the expected diagnostic value of examination justifies them. The escalation threshold is stated rather than left to preference.
policies.M019:c05: Require in-person assessment wherever hands-on findings could materially change management, on the ground that diagnostic responsibility outweighs convenience, while the service absorbs the burden by offering local or out-of-hours slots.
policies.M019:c06: Assess remotely at once and schedule an in-person reassessment that happens unless predefined improvement thresholds are met, so that video is a first step rather than the definitive assessment, and the reassessment is booked rather than offered.
policies.M020:c01: Assign outbreak work fairly across those qualified, with exemptions confined to extraordinary personal risk, defined in advance and decided by someone other than the assigning manager. The rota and the exemptions granted are visible to staff.
policies.M020:c02: Make outbreak service voluntary, with broad exemption for serious personal, household or caregiving vulnerability, and use reassignment and incentives to fill the rota rather than compulsion. Declining is recorded without consequence for the clinician's standing.
policies.M020:c03: Hold clinicians to a strong professional duty once protection, training and monitoring are adequate, with narrow individualised exemptions assessed case by case. The institution must first demonstrate that the protective conditions are actually met.
policies.M020:c04: Set the obligation individually against each clinician's own risk and circumstances, with reassignment and exemption available more broadly for vulnerability, and the assessment repeated as the outbreak and the person's situation change.
policies.M020:c05: Use a fair mandatory rotation grounded in shared obligation, entered only after the institution has minimised risk as far as it can, with the rotation published, the burden shared across seniority, and the risk reduction demonstrated rather than asserted.
policies.M020:c06: Make assignment voluntary with broad vulnerability exemptions, on the ground that clinicians have duties to themselves and their dependants and that what may be demanded is proportionate to the protection provided.
policies.M021:c01: Continue intensive treatment while the parents request it and meaningful benefit remains medically possible, with reassessment at defined intervals rather than on request. Each reassessment records what has changed and is shared with the parents at the time.
policies.M021:c02: Agree a time-limited trial with clinical goals set before it begins — what would count as improvement, by when — then reassess with the parents against those goals rather than against how the team feels the child is doing.
policies.M021:c03: Recommend transition to comfort care while leaving the decision with the parents anywhere within the medically reasonable range, stating clearly where that range ends and what lies outside it.
policies.M021:c04: Permit forgoing treatment judged non-beneficial despite a continuing parental request, but only after a second opinion, ethics review, a genuine opportunity to transfer, and a due-process interval the parents were told about in advance.
policies.M021:c05: Give parents strong presumptive authority, on the ground that they carry special responsibility for the newborn and that the prognosis is uncertain. The presumption yields only to evidence that treatment has become harmful rather than merely burdensome.
policies.M021:c06: Make the child's balance of benefit and burden controlling once treatment mainly prolongs suffering or dying, with that judgment made explicitly, recorded, and confirmed by a clinician outside the treating team.
policies.M021:c07: Require extended accommodation and real transfer efforts before any unilateral withdrawal, on the ground that moral injury and prognostic uncertainty warrant institutional restraint. What counts as a real transfer effort is defined rather than left to judgment.
policies.M021:c08: Continue treatment while the parents request it and their questions remain unanswered, with family meetings scheduled at set intervals rather than an open-ended wait, so that parents are not asked to decide before they understand the prognosis.
policies.M022:c01: Counsel in a balanced way across the gray zone and let the parents choose among the medically reasonable options, including comfort care, with the choice revisited at birth against the infant's actual condition rather than treated as fixed antenatally.
policies.M022:c02: Presume active resuscitation wherever survival remains materially possible, unless informed parents choose comfort care, with the presumption stated in advance and the parents' choice recorded before delivery where time allows.
policies.M022:c03: Presume comfort-focused care at the lowest part of the viability range unless informed parents affirmatively request resuscitation, with the range defined by the unit in advance and the request recorded.
policies.M022:c04: Begin a time-limited trial of resuscitation at birth and redirect according to the infant's actual condition and response, with the assessment points and what would prompt redirection agreed with the parents beforehand.
policies.M022:c05: Use gestational and clinical thresholds to narrow the preference-sensitive zone, leaving parental discretion only inside it, and publish the thresholds so that families and clinicians know before delivery where discretion begins and ends.
policies.M022:c06: Give survival and continued life greater weight where parents prioritise the possibility of life despite disability and uncertainty, with the disability outcomes described concretely rather than as a general warning.
policies.M022:c07: Give avoidance of invasive suffering greater weight where parents prioritise comfort, with the burdens of intensive care described concretely and comfort care offered as a full plan rather than as the absence of treatment.
policies.M023:c01: Pursue expanded access where the regulatory criteria are met, monitoring is in place, and the benefit-to-burden threshold is satisfied, with each of those three recorded before the request and reviewed if the child's condition changes.
policies.M023:c02: Decline access where expected benefit is too low relative to burden, or where access would undermine the integrity of the trial or the development programme, stating which ground applies and what would change it.
policies.M023:c03: Offer a time-limited monitored trial with stopping criteria set in advance, where uncertainty is high but some benefit remains plausible, and stop when those criteria are met rather than when the family is ready.
policies.M023:c04: Give parents substantial rescue discretion after transparent counselling, on the ground that no standard option remains, provided the counselling states plainly that the intervention may not work and may cause harm.
policies.M023:c05: Protect the child from burdensome low-probability intervention where suffering is high and benefit speculative, with that judgment made by the treating team, recorded, and explained to the family with the alternative plan.
policies.M023:c06: Require independent review before exceptional access, covering fairness, scientific plausibility, conflicts of interest, and consistency with how other families' requests have been handled, with the review completed within a stated period.
policies.M023:c07: Give the family a written answer with a named decision-maker and a date, so that a request for access is answered rather than absorbed into the treatment discussion, and the answer states what would change a refusal.
policies.M024:c01: Permit puberty-related medical intervention after multidisciplinary assessment of persistence, capacity, co-occurring conditions and the balance of benefits and harms, with the young person and parents involved throughout and the reasoning recorded.
policies.M024:c02: Restrict puberty suppression to research or specialist protocols while the evidence remains substantially uncertain, with the protocol collecting outcomes and the restriction reviewed as evidence accumulates rather than standing indefinitely.
policies.M024:c03: Defer non-reversible hormonal intervention until adulthood or a higher evidentiary threshold, while providing psychosocial and non-medical support throughout, so that deferral is a plan of care rather than a refusal of it.
policies.M024:c04: Use individualised shared decision-making without categorical age or service bans, stating plainly that the evidence is low-certainty and what that means for this decision, and recording the young person's own account of their preference.
policies.M024:c05: Apply a precautionary threshold in which greater irreversibility and greater evidentiary uncertainty each require stronger evidence before proceeding, with the two dimensions assessed separately and the threshold written down.
policies.M024:c06: Give substantial weight to the adolescent's autonomy and to the harms of unwanted pubertal development where capacity and a sustained preference are established, with sustained meaning documented over a stated period rather than at one visit.
policies.M024:c07: Begin with reversible support and scheduled reassessment, escalating only as goals, capacity and evidence justify, with each step and its review date agreed in advance rather than decided at the point of escalation.
policies.M024:c08: Keep the young person and their family in specialist care with scheduled review whatever is decided about medication, so that deferral is not experienced as discharge, and the next appointment is booked before the decision is communicated.
policies.M025:c01: Respect informed parental deferral while guaranteeing fluent sign-language access from the outset and a scheduled audiological reconsideration, so that deferral does not become drift and language development is not delayed while the decision is open.
policies.M025:c02: Favour timely implantation where family goals prioritise auditory and spoken-language opportunity, while maintaining sign-language and developmental support alongside it rather than as a fallback if implantation disappoints.
policies.M025:c03: Use interdisciplinary family-centred candidacy assessment and recommend timely implantation where indicated, integrating the family's goals, the child's language exposure and developmental profile, with the recommendation and its basis given to the family in writing.
policies.M025:c04: Respect Deaf cultural and linguistic parental authority absent serious harm, with serious harm defined by the child's language and developmental outcomes rather than by hearing status, and reviewed against milestones.
policies.M025:c05: Strongly favour timely implantation to preserve the child's future auditory option, while guaranteeing sign language in parallel, on the ground that keeping both open costs less than closing either.
policies.M025:c06: Use milestone-based watchful waiting with explicit language and developmental criteria for reconsideration, agreed with parents who remain uncertain, so that the decision returns automatically at defined points rather than only if the family raises it.
policies.M026:c01: Continue treatment while intensive communication, a second opinion, ethics review and goals clarification proceed, with each step scheduled rather than open-ended and the family told when the process will conclude.
policies.M026:c02: Agree a time-limited trial with clinical endpoints set before it begins — what would count as improvement and by when — and decide continuation or withdrawal against those endpoints rather than against the team's overall impression.
policies.M026:c03: After fair process and a genuine opportunity to transfer, permit withdrawal of treatment judged potentially inappropriate despite continuing surrogate objection, with the process steps completed and recorded and the decision reviewed outside the treating team.
policies.M026:c04: Continue treatment while the surrogate's interpretation of the patient's values remains plausible and the burdens are not overwhelming, with plausibility assessed against what is known of the patient rather than against the team's own view of the outcome.
policies.M026:c05: Make benefit, burden and professional integrity controlling once treatment no longer advances any acceptable patient-centred goal, with the goals stated explicitly and the finding that none remains achievable recorded and independently confirmed.
policies.M026:c06: Require a transfer to a willing institution before any unilateral withdrawal wherever that is feasible, with the search documented, the institutions contacted named, and support continued while it proceeds.
policies.M026:c07: Permit a longer accommodation period for religious or moral objection where doing so does not impose disproportionate burdens on the patient or the service, with the extension stated as a period and the burdens assessed rather than assumed.
policies.M026:c08: Fix the accommodation period in advance and tell the family what it is, so that time is a stated part of the plan rather than something they must keep asking for, with the end date recorded and any extension explained.
policies.M027:c01: Follow the applicable prior directive even where the person now appears content, on the ground that the capable person's earlier choice governs, provided the directive addresses this situation and its applicability is recorded rather than assumed.
policies.M027:c02: Give the person's current experience and their present assent or dissent priority once they can no longer endorse the earlier directive, reading behaviour as well as words and recording what was observed and by whom.
policies.M027:c03: Give the prior directive strong presumptive weight while allowing it to be overridden where present wellbeing is substantial and the burden-benefit balance differs materially from what the person anticipated, with the difference named rather than asserted.
policies.M027:c04: Interpret the directive through the person's broader values rather than its literal wording, using substituted judgment where the values are known, and recording the interpretation so that it can be examined and revised.
policies.M027:c05: Honour present resistance to burdensome treatment even where the earlier directive would permit it, so that precedent autonomy is not used to compel an intervention the person is now refusing in the only way available to them.
policies.M027:c06: Use a time-limited treatment trial where prognosis and current quality of life are uncertain, then reassess against both the person's prior values and their present welfare, with the reassessment date fixed at the start.
policies.M027:c07: Require independent review where the literal directive and the person's current apparent interests sharply conflict, with the review recording why one temporal self's interests were preferred rather than treating the conflict as resolved by the document.
policies.M027:c08: Ask the family what the person said while they could still say it, record that alongside the directive, and revisit it whenever the plan changes, so that the account is built up over time rather than recalled once.
policies.M028:c01: Continue organ support for a meaningful accommodation period where an informed family rejects the determination, while transfer or resolution proceeds, with the period stated at the outset and the family told what happens at its end.
policies.M028:c02: Provide support and a reasonable transition period, without any commitment to indefinite continuation, with the transition length stated in advance and the reasons for it explained rather than left to negotiation.
policies.M028:c03: Provide a limited accommodation period with a defined disagreement process, then discontinue unless another authorised pathway exists, with the period and the process published as institutional policy rather than set case by case.
policies.M028:c04: Provide substantial conscience accommodation where feasible, on the ground that forced discontinuation can cause profound moral injury, with feasibility assessed against staffing and other patients' needs and the assessment recorded.
policies.M028:c05: Limit accommodation on the ground that clinicians should not provide indefinite organ support after death and that resources are owed to living patients, with the limit stated in advance rather than reached when pressure mounts.
policies.M028:c06: Treat transfer as the presumptive route once family rejection persists beyond the accommodation period, continuing support only while transfer remains actively feasible, with feasibility reviewed at stated intervals.
policies.M029:c01: Sedate proportionally at the lowest depth that relieves the refractory symptom, with reassessment at short intervals and titration up or down as the symptom changes, recorded each time.
policies.M029:c02: Permit continuous deep sedation where lighter sedation cannot adequately relieve refractory suffering and the patient has given informed consent, with the failure of lighter sedation documented rather than presumed.
policies.M029:c03: Begin with intermittent or time-limited sedation before continuous deep sedation where the symptom pattern and the patient's goals make a reversible trial feasible, with the trial's length and purpose agreed with the patient beforehand.
policies.M029:c04: Honour a capable dying patient's informed preference for deeper continuous sedation once suffering is refractory, even where a lighter level might technically reduce symptoms, with the preference recorded in the patient's own words.
policies.M029:c05: Use the minimum effective depth, on the ground that preserving consciousness and the possibility of interaction has value where symptom relief can still be achieved, with each increase justified by a symptom that lighter sedation did not control.
policies.M029:c06: Decline sedation intended primarily to hasten death, while distinguishing that intention from proportionate symptom relief that may foreseeably affect consciousness or survival, with the intention recorded through the dosing and titration rationale.
policies.M029:c07: Involve family in the decision only to the extent the patient wishes, and do not let family distress alone determine the depth of sedation, with the patient's wishes about involvement recorded while they can still state them.
policies.M030:c01: Provide hospice support alongside selected disease-directed treatment, with the treatments that may continue named in advance and reviewed as goals change, rather than requiring the patient to choose between the two.
policies.M030:c02: Offer a distinct comfort-focused hospice pathway, with what it includes and excludes stated plainly at enrolment so that the choice is understood before it is made.
policies.M030:c03: Use a traditional hospice election in which the patient forgoes disease-directed treatment for the terminal condition, with the boundary of that condition defined and the election revocable.
policies.M030:c04: Use a concurrent-care architecture in which hospice and disease-directed treatment are funded together, with eligibility criteria published and the two services coordinated rather than parallel.
policies.M030:c05: Provide concurrent care on autonomy and non-abandonment grounds, so that accepting hospice never requires giving up treatment the patient still wants, with the commitment stated at enrolment.
policies.M030:c06: Keep the hospice benefit bounded and distinct on stewardship and coherence grounds, with the boundary defined by the terminal condition and the reasoning explained to patients rather than presented as a rule without one.
policies.M031:c01: Permit clinician participation where capacity, terminal prognosis and voluntariness are established and the statutory safeguards are met, with each element assessed independently and recorded, and the assessments repeated before the act.
policies.M031:c02: Prohibit physician participation while guaranteeing full palliative care, with the palliative alternative offered in practice — specialist access, symptom control, continuity — rather than named as a reason for the prohibition.
policies.M031:c03: Take no institutional position while providing for individual conscience and a working transfer and access process, with the transfer arranged by the institution and the timeline stated.
policies.M031:c04: Require a referral or access pathway where the practice is lawful, with the pathway named, contactable, and effective within the patient's clinical window rather than left to the patient to locate.
policies.M031:c05: Permit access on grounds of autonomy and relief of suffering, with the request originating from the patient and the assessment recording their own reasons rather than a clinical summary of them.
policies.M031:c06: Prohibit participation on grounds of professional role and non-maleficence, with the prohibition applying to the act rather than to discussing it, so that patients can still raise the question and be heard.
policies.M031:c07: Add safeguards addressing disability, coercion, socioeconomic pressure and access to palliative care, assessed explicitly in every case and recorded, with a request deferred where any of them is unresolved.
policies.M032:c01: Permit only under exceptional due-care criteria with independent psychiatric review, with the reviewer independent of the treating team and of the assessing physician, and the review recorded in full.
policies.M032:c02: Require an extended treatment history, a second opinion, and a finding that no reasonable alternative remains, with reasonable alternative defined by what is actually available to this patient rather than what exists in principle.
policies.M032:c03: Exclude psychiatric-only suffering from eligibility, stating the exclusion as a categorical rule so that patients are not assessed under a standard that cannot be met, while guaranteeing continued treatment.
policies.M032:c04: Route every psychiatric case through central specialist review, with the reviewing body constituted in advance, its criteria published, and its decisions recorded for consistency across cases.
policies.M032:c05: Do not exclude capable patients on the basis of diagnosis alone, on autonomy and equality grounds, requiring any refusal to name a feature of this patient's decision rather than of their condition.
policies.M032:c06: Apply exceptional precaution or exclusion on grounds of vulnerability and prognostic uncertainty, with the uncertainty stated — what cannot be known about the course of this illness — rather than asserted generally.
policies.M032:c07: Defer for a stated period with renewed assessment after further treatment opportunities, with the treatments named, made available, and the reassessment automatic rather than requiring a fresh request.
policies.M032:c08: Guarantee continued treatment and support throughout any assessment, so that asking to be assessed never reduces the care a person is offered, with the treating team's obligations unchanged and stated in writing.
policies.M033:c01: Allow a valid advance directive to substitute for a current oral request where every due-care criterion is met, with the directive's applicability to the present situation established and recorded by an independent assessor.
policies.M033:c02: Require some current communicative confirmation or observable concurrence before proceeding, with what would count defined in advance rather than judged in the moment, and the absence of it treated as decisive.
policies.M033:c03: Permit only where the directive is specific, was repeatedly confirmed while the person was capable, current suffering and applicability are established, and independent review agrees, with all four recorded separately.
policies.M033:c04: Do not proceed where present behaviour suggests resistance or where the directive's applicability is materially uncertain, with resistance interpreted broadly and any doubt resolved against proceeding.
policies.M033:c05: Let precedent autonomy control, on the ground that the capable person's settled choice about their own dying is theirs to make, with the directive's specificity and its confirmations documented.
policies.M033:c06: Let present experiential interests and current minimal autonomy control, treating the person now as the one whose life is at stake, with their present state assessed by those who know them.
policies.M033:c07: Require independent multidisciplinary adjudication wherever the directive and the person's current state conflict, with the adjudication recording why one was preferred and what evidence decided it.
policies.M034:c01: Continue clinically assisted nutrition and hydration while diagnosis and prognosis are clarified and the family deliberates, with the clarification following a defined assessment schedule rather than continuing indefinitely.
policies.M034:c02: Withdraw after a best-interests process shared with the family where burdens and prognosis justify it, with the assessment recording what is known of the person's values and what remains unknown.
policies.M034:c03: Continue for a defined period with reassessment milestones set in advance, agreed with the family, and applied at those points rather than deferred when they arrive.
policies.M034:c04: Continue where the family reasonably interprets the person's values as favouring preservation of life under uncertainty, with that interpretation recorded and tested against what is known rather than accepted or dismissed.
policies.M034:c05: Withdraw where the family reasonably interprets the person's values as rejecting prolonged dependence and burdensome intervention, with the interpretation recorded and independently reviewed before an irreversible step.
policies.M034:c06: Require independent neurorehabilitation and ethics review before irreversible withdrawal wherever diagnosis or prognosis is contested, with the contest identified explicitly and the review addressing it.
policies.M035:c01: Respect a decision to stop eating and drinking after assessing capacity, coercion and symptoms, and provide anticipatory symptom care — mouth care, sedation for distress, family support — arranged before it begins.
policies.M035:c02: Treat reversible depression, uncontrolled symptoms, misinformation or coercion before accepting the decision as settled, with each addressed and the decision revisited afterwards rather than accepted at first statement.
policies.M035:c03: Allow conscientious non-participation while guaranteeing non-abandonment, transfer and symptom relief, with an alternative clinician arranged and the patient's care unchanged in the interim.
policies.M035:c04: Support hospice and family with clear expectations about the course and duration and with the caregiver resources that sustain it, provided in advance rather than as the need becomes acute.
policies.M035:c05: Accompany the person on autonomy grounds, providing symptom care without pressure to resume, with the accompaniment recorded as the plan rather than as acquiescence.
policies.M035:c06: Continue efforts to restore the desire to eat and drink where that is ethically and legally permissible, with those efforts bounded, non-coercive, and stopped when the person's decision remains settled.
policies.M036:c01: Treat withholding and withdrawing as ethically equivalent once the intervention no longer serves the patient's goals, and require the same justification for each rather than a higher one for stopping.
policies.M036:c02: Require a higher procedural threshold for withdrawal, on the ground that stopping an established treatment engages reliance and causal concerns, with the additional steps specified rather than left to local practice.
policies.M036:c03: Use explicit time-limited trials so that starting does not create a presumption of continuing, with the endpoint and the review agreed before the treatment begins and recorded where the family can see them.
policies.M036:c04: Where uncertainty is high, start treatment with stopping criteria rather than withhold, on the ground that reversibility preserves options, with the criteria fixed at the outset and applied when met.
policies.M036:c05: Avoid starting where later withdrawal would be psychologically or institutionally harder and expected benefit is low, with that judgment made explicitly and shared with the family rather than left as a reason not offered.
policies.M036:c06: Choose between formal equivalence and a rule that treats acts, omissions and reliance as morally distinct, and state which is being applied in this case so that the reasoning is available for challenge.
policies.M037:c01: Do not offer an escalation that cannot reasonably achieve the agreed goal, after explaining transparently what the goal is and why the escalation cannot meet it, with the explanation given in writing.
policies.M037:c02: Obtain a second opinion, ethics review and an appeal opportunity before any final non-offer where disagreement persists, with the timeline stated and the surrogate told how to use each step.
policies.M037:c03: Offer a time-limited trial where benefit is uncertain rather than effectively absent, with the distinction stated and the stopping criteria agreed before the trial begins.
policies.M037:c04: Maintain eligibility temporarily while transfer to a willing centre is explored, with the search documented and support continued while it remains realistic.
policies.M037:c05: Give the surrogate's request presumptive weight where some plausible goal-concordant benefit remains, with plausibility assessed against the agreed goal and the assessment recorded.
policies.M037:c06: Permit a firm non-offer on grounds of professional integrity and non-maleficence where the escalation cannot meet the goal, with that finding made institutionally rather than by the bedside team alone.
policies.M037:c07: Tell the surrogate in writing, at the time of the request, what will and will not be offered and why, naming the route to a second opinion and the person who will handle it.
policies.M038:c01: Follow the deceased person's known prior wishes about postmortem somatic support and pregnancy, with those wishes established from a document or a recorded conversation rather than from a general impression.
policies.M038:c02: Let the surrogate or family decide where prior wishes are unknown and fetal survival is plausible, with plausibility stated as a clinical estimate and the decision revisited as that estimate changes.
policies.M038:c03: Continue support to a defined gestational threshold where prognosis is reasonable and burdens proportionate, with the threshold set at the outset and the burdens on the family reviewed as it approaches.
policies.M038:c04: Discontinue on the ground that the person is dead and continued use of their body conflicts with their autonomy and dignity absent prior authorisation, with the absence of authorisation established rather than assumed.
policies.M038:c05: Permit continuation only after independent maternal-fetal and ethics review of fetal prognosis, burdens, resources and the person's prior values, with the review completed before support is committed rather than after.
policies.M038:c06: Allow substantial family accommodation without indefinite support, ending it where fetal benefit becomes negligible, with the point at which that is judged defined in advance and explained to the family.
policies.M039:c01: Offer donation to medically suitable competent patients only after the assisted-dying decision is independently established, with separate teams, first-person consent, an unconditional right to withdraw, and compliance with the dead-donor rule.
policies.M039:c02: Raise donation only after the patient initiates it or at a defined neutral point, with that point fixed in policy so that the timing cannot be adjusted toward a donation outcome.
policies.M039:c03: Decline donation where premortem procedures or logistics would impose burdens the donor has not separately authorised, with each such procedure consented to specifically rather than covered by a general agreement.
policies.M039:c04: Facilitate donation on autonomy grounds, treating the patient's wish to donate as theirs to act on, with the arrangements made without altering the assisted-dying process.
policies.M039:c05: Require strict separation of care teams and decisions on public-trust grounds, with the separation structural rather than procedural and stated publicly so that it can be relied on.
policies.M039:c06: Permit clinician conscience opt-out while the institution guarantees continuity and transfer, with the alternative clinician identified in advance rather than sought when the objection arises.
policies.M039:c07: Let the patient raise donation whenever they wish and answer fully, without allowing the donation question to alter the timing or handling of the assisted-dying decision, and record that the two were kept separate.
policies.M040:c01: Proceed after clear communication, on the ground that determining death is a professional responsibility rather than something requiring family authorisation, with the communication documented and support offered throughout.
policies.M040:c02: Allow a brief accommodation period for family understanding and religious support before testing where that is clinically feasible, with the period stated and the reason for any limit explained.
policies.M040:c03: Require family permission for apnoea testing specifically, on the ground that it carries procedural risk and profound significance, while other components of the determination proceed.
policies.M040:c04: Use ancillary testing in place of apnoea testing where objection or clinical risk makes that a valid guideline pathway, with the substitution recorded and the guideline basis named.
policies.M040:c05: Proceed over objection only after a second opinion and ethics or legal review, with each completed and recorded before testing rather than sought afterwards.
policies.M040:c06: Transfer where feasible if another institution can accommodate the objection without departing from accepted death-determination standards, with the search documented and support continued while it proceeds.
policies.M040:c07: Explain what the testing involves and why before it happens, and allow a short defined period for the family to gather, rather than proceeding on the clinical timetable alone, with the period stated at the time.
policies.M041:c01: Prioritise by expected live-birth rate, using a stated prognostic model applied identically to every applicant, with the model published and audited for whether it entrenches existing disadvantage.
policies.M041:c02: Allocate by lottery among all who meet a minimum eligibility standard, with eligibility defined clinically, the draw run openly, and unsuccessful applicants told they may re-enter.
policies.M041:c03: Combine urgency and time-sensitivity, prior access and distributive criteria under a published rule stating the weight of each, applied by a panel rather than at referral.
policies.M041:c04: Allocate first-come first-served among eligible applicants, with the queue recorded and the eligibility assessment made promptly so that referral speed does not decide access.
policies.M041:c05: Fund more people at lower expected success rather than maximising total births, stating the trade-off in births foregone rather than presenting it as costless.
policies.M041:c06: Reject exclusions based on family status or social worth, with the eligibility criteria stated exhaustively so that no informal criterion can operate alongside them.
policies.M041:c07: Allocate where expected benefit per funded cycle is highest, with the calculation published and its distributional effects reported alongside the efficiency gain.
policies.M042:c01: Offer screening universally with balanced information about the condition and about living with it, prepared with disabled people and given before the test is booked.
policies.M042:c02: Require explicit opt-in after values-oriented counselling, with the counselling offered at a time that allows reflection and its content specified rather than left to the clinician.
policies.M042:c03: Confine testing to serious health conditions and resist expansion to traits, with the boundary defined in the programme's policy and any addition requiring public justification.
policies.M042:c04: Make disability-inclusive counselling, including lived-experience and support information, a required component of informed choice, with the materials co-produced and their use audited.
policies.M042:c05: Make screening available non-directively, emphasising the patient's own reproductive choice, with the neutrality of the materials checked rather than assumed from their tone.
policies.M042:c06: Impose programme-level limits where routinisation would predictably increase stigma or erode services, with that prediction assessed on evidence and the limits reviewed as services change.
policies.M042:c07: Offer universally with standardised neutral information and no mandatory values session, with the information reviewed for balance and a values conversation available on request.
policies.M043:c01: Provide non-directive counselling and access, with the decision left to the patient, the counselling covering continuation as fully as reduction, and no clinician preference recorded as advice.
policies.M043:c02: Recommend reduction strongly above a defined maternal or fetal risk threshold while leaving the final choice to the patient, with the threshold stated and the recommendation recorded as such.
policies.M043:c03: Continue the pregnancy with intensive high-risk care where the patient declines reduction, with the care plan specified and resourced rather than framed as making the best of a refusal.
policies.M043:c04: Restrict reduction requested solely for non-medical preference below a specified fetal number or risk threshold, with the threshold published so that patients know it before treatment begins.
policies.M043:c05: Favour patient control on autonomy grounds, with any restriction required to identify a harm to someone other than the patient.
policies.M043:c06: Favour reduction where the expected reduction in morbidity is large, with that expectation stated numerically and the patient's own risk tolerance recorded.
policies.M043:c07: Provide the counselling and, where chosen, the procedure at the centre already managing the pregnancy, so that acting on the decision does not require travel or repeating the history. Where the centre cannot provide it, the referral is arranged with the records transferred and the appointment booked before the patient leaves.
policies.M044:c01: Offer the procedure to selected informed candidates meeting published programme criteria, with the criteria and the programme's own outcomes made available before assessment begins.
policies.M044:c02: Restrict the procedure to prospective registry or research protocols at expert centres, with the registry mandatory, its data published, and the restriction reviewed against accumulating outcomes.
policies.M044:c03: Decline routine provision on the ground that the transplant, donor and pregnancy burdens are disproportionate for a benefit that is not life-saving, with that comparison stated rather than assumed.
policies.M044:c04: Prefer the deceased-donor pathway wherever feasible to avoid living-donor harm, with feasibility assessed for each case and the preference stated in the programme's protocol.
policies.M044:c05: Recognise gestational parenthood as a substantial interest on reproductive-autonomy grounds, with the weight it carries stated rather than left implicit in the decision to offer.
policies.M044:c06: Give high weight to recipient and donor surgical and immunosuppression risks, with those risks quantified from the programme's own and published outcomes rather than described generally.
policies.M044:c07: Compare the programme transparently with other transplant and reproductive priorities, with the comparison published, rather than assuming infertility treatment is either trivial or equivalent to life-saving transplantation.
policies.M044:c08: Publish what the programme offers, its outcomes so far and its selection criteria, so that patients can judge for themselves whether to seek it, updated as the programme's results accumulate.
policies.M045:c01: Permit use only where the deceased gave written authorisation, with the authorisation specific to posthumous use and its terms followed as written.
policies.M045:c02: Permit a surviving spouse or partner to use the material without a written directive only where strong evidence shows the deceased's reproductive wishes and nothing contradicts them, with the evidence assessed independently.
policies.M045:c03: Permit no use at all absent explicit authorisation, with the rule stated at the time of storage so that people know what happens if they do not record a decision.
policies.M045:c04: Honour a specific prior prohibition even where the survivor wants use, with the prohibition applied as written and not weighed against the survivor's circumstances.
policies.M045:c05: Give the deceased's prior intent priority on precedent-autonomy grounds, with the intent established from what they recorded rather than from what those who knew them believe.
policies.M045:c06: Permit use where a jointly formed reproductive plan is strongly evidenced and no objection exists, with the evidence documented and the absence of objection established rather than assumed.
policies.M046:c01: Provide the service broadly within clinical and legal limits, with the limits stated publicly and provision resourced so that availability is real rather than nominal.
policies.M046:c02: Provide a narrower range directly while guaranteeing timely referral or transfer for what is not offered, with the receiving service named and the transfer arranged by the hospital.
policies.M046:c03: Provide only urgent medically necessary care and refer for the rest, with the referral pathway named, funded, and its timeliness monitored against the clinical window.
policies.M046:c04: Permit hospital-level conscience accommodation only where equivalent timely access is institutionally guaranteed, with the guarantee demonstrated in practice and audited.
policies.M046:c05: Favour integrated mainstream provision on access-justice and professional-duty grounds, treating the service as part of ordinary care rather than as a specialised exception.
policies.M046:c06: Permit a narrower service identity while imposing non-abandonment and access duties, with those duties specified and their fulfilment reported rather than assumed.
policies.M046:c07: Publish what the hospital does and does not provide, so that a patient knows before arriving rather than at the point of need, with the information given to referrers as well as patients.
policies.M047:c01: Provide after ordinary non-judgmental shared decision-making, with no age or parity veto, and with the same process that would apply to any other elective procedure.
policies.M047:c02: Use longitudinal counselling or an optional return visit to support sustained deliberation, offered rather than required, so that delay is available to the patient without being imposed on them.
policies.M047:c03: Require an independent second clinical review for unusually young or nulliparous requests, with the trigger stated in policy and the review's role limited to confirming the process rather than the choice.
policies.M047:c04: Apply a uniform cooling-off interval before elective permanent contraception, with the interval the same for every patient regardless of age or parity and its length stated in advance.
policies.M047:c05: Defer or decline below a defined age or parity threshold on grounds of anticipated regret, with the threshold published and the evidence for the regret estimate stated.
