policies.M047:c06: Give the competent patient's reproductive values primary authority while screening for coercion and for demographic bias in who is questioned, with that screening applied to the clinician's practice as well as the patient.
policies.M047:c07: Permit proportionate deliberative safeguards for an irreversible decision while rejecting permanent demographic vetoes, with the safeguards applied uniformly and their effect on access monitored.
policies.M047:c08: Provide the procedure on the same terms as for any other adult, without an added waiting period, second review or parity threshold that would not apply to an older or parenting patient. Any safeguard the service does apply is written into policy and applied to every patient, so that it cannot be introduced for this one.
policies.M048:c01: Require the contemporaneous consent of both contributors for reproductive use, so that a prior agreement does not authorise use over a present objection.
policies.M048:c02: Enforce a sufficiently specific prior disposition agreement unless both parties revise it, with specificity defined by whether the agreement addresses this circumstance.
policies.M048:c03: Default against reproductive use where either genetic contributor currently objects, with the default stated at storage so that both know it before creating embryos.
policies.M048:c04: Permit use by one former partner where the prior agreement clearly authorised it and the embryos are that person's only realistic route to genetic parenthood, with both conditions established independently.
policies.M048:c05: Require advance choices with periodic reconfirmation while both retain control, with reconfirmation at each renewal and a stated consequence if one party does not respond.
policies.M048:c06: Resolve ambiguity by permitting no reproductive use, while allowing mutually authorised discard or donation, with the ambiguity identified explicitly rather than resolved in favour of the more insistent party.
policies.M048:c07: Put the disposition agreement in front of both people again at each storage renewal, so that what happens on disagreement is settled while both still agree. Each renewal records both signatures and the current choice, and storage does not continue on the strength of an agreement neither has looked at for years.
policies.M049:c01: Continue storage for a long defined period before any default disposal, with the period stated at the outset and contact attempted at intervals throughout it.
policies.M049:c02: Thaw or discard after a defined contact and notice period, with the notice sent by stated means, the attempts recorded, and a final period allowed after the last attempt.
policies.M049:c03: Transfer storage responsibility and fees under a contract agreed in advance, with the terms explained at storage rather than invoked when payment stops.
policies.M049:c04: Prohibit research or reproductive donation absent specific prior authorisation, with the prohibition applying to every use other than the disposition the contributors chose.
policies.M049:c05: Require an explicit default-disposition choice at storage and at each renewal, so that unclaimed status is prevented rather than resolved, with the choice recorded and confirmable.
policies.M049:c06: Treat storage without instruction as a duty owed to the people who created the embryos: act only after the notice they were promised has genuinely been given, and follow the disposition they last recorded. What counts as genuine notice — the means, the number of attempts, the interval — is fixed at the outset rather than judged when fees stop.
policies.M050:c01: Release donor identity to the donor-conceived person at adulthood as of right, with the arrangement stated to donors before donation and the register maintained to make it effective.
policies.M050:c02: Provide non-identifying information as of right and identity or contact only where both parties consent, with the mutual-consent register maintained and both told it exists.
policies.M050:c03: Preserve anonymity as promised while telling donors and recipients plainly that consumer DNA testing makes practical secrecy unreliable, with that warning given before donation.
policies.M050:c04: Maintain a permanent channel for medical and genetic updates in both directions regardless of identity release, with the channel funded and the obligation to use it explained to donors.
policies.M050:c05: Favour access at maturity on the ground that donor-conceived people have an interest in their own origins, with support offered around the disclosure rather than only the record.
policies.M050:c06: Protect the terms under which donation occurred, on reliance grounds, with any change applying prospectively and past donors told what has and has not changed.
policies.M050:c07: Offer donors a prospective choice among identifiable, mutual-consent and limited-information donation, with the downstream consequences of each stated plainly before they choose.
policies.M051:c01: Permit use for severe monogenic disease under stringent national and international oversight, with the conditions covered listed, the oversight body constituted before any application, and its decisions published.
policies.M051:c02: Permit only where preimplantation testing and other reasonable alternatives cannot reliably avoid the disease, with that finding made for the specific couple and independently confirmed.
policies.M051:c03: Maintain the reproductive prohibition while permitting laboratory research, with the boundary defined by transfer rather than by technique, and research subject to its own oversight.
policies.M051:c04: Permit broader reproductive choice for serious disease once safety is adequate, with adequacy defined by stated evidence rather than by regulatory readiness, and the definition published in advance.
policies.M051:c05: Require multigenerational follow-up and a registry as a condition of any permission, with participation mandatory, funded, and the results published across generations.
policies.M051:c06: Condition access on fair distribution and on a boundary against enhancement, with both defined in advance and access monitored so that the technology does not become available only to those who can pay.
policies.M051:c07: Prohibit germline modification categorically even after technical readiness, on the ground that future persons and species-level change cannot be appropriately authorised by present decision-makers.
policies.M051:c08: Involve affected families and people living with the condition in setting the criteria, and publish the outcome of that involvement alongside any decision to permit or refuse, including where their view did not prevail.
policies.M052:c01: Prohibit ranking embryos on non-medical traits, with the prohibition applying to the service offered rather than to the underlying data, and stated in the clinic's published policy.
policies.M052:c02: Confine the technique to research until stated evidence thresholds are met, with the thresholds specified as predictive performance across ancestry groups and the restriction reviewed against them.
policies.M052:c03: Permit validated serious health-risk applications while excluding height, cognition and similar traits, with the permitted conditions listed and additions requiring public justification.
policies.M052:c04: Permit informed reproductive choice for validated traits, with validation defined by stated performance criteria and the limits of prediction explained to patients before selection.
policies.M052:c05: Restrict on the ground that stratification and unequal predictive performance across ancestries create population-level harms, with those effects assessed rather than asserted.
policies.M052:c06: Permit only where validity and equity thresholds are met across ancestry groups, with performance reported by group and the service withdrawn where it is not.
policies.M052:c07: Permit the clinic to decline trait selection as inconsistent with its purpose even where it is lawful, with the policy published before treatment begins so that patients are not surprised by it.
policies.M053:c01: Permit competent parental reproductive choice for enhancement judged safe, with safety established by stated evidence and the choice made after counselling that states what remains unknown.
policies.M053:c02: Permit only interventions that restore or prevent serious disease or maintain normal functioning, with the boundary defined by a stated clinical criterion rather than by the wording of the request.
policies.M053:c03: Prohibit reproductive enhancement categorically, with the prohibition applying to the intervention rather than the motive, and stated in law rather than in clinic policy.
policies.M053:c04: Permit limited enhancement only where access is equitable and social externalities are controlled, with both conditions specified, monitored, and the permission withdrawn if they fail.
policies.M053:c05: Restrict on precautionary grounds because the effects on future generations and on social competition remain uncertain despite technical safety, naming the uncertainties so the position can be revisited.
policies.M053:c06: Bar selection that entrenches hierarchy or drives positional competition, with the assessment made for the specific trait and setting rather than for enhancement in general.
policies.M053:c07: Decide by public deliberation with a published result rather than by clinic-level discretion, so that access does not turn on which programme a family happens to reach, with the decision binding on all providers.
policies.M054:c01: Analyse and return a defined list of actionable findings, with an opt-out offered before sequencing, the list published, and any change to it explained to patients already sequenced.
policies.M054:c02: Require opt-in before any secondary analysis, with the choice made before the sample is analysed and the categories described concretely enough to choose between them.
policies.M054:c03: Return only findings of very high actionability and penetrance, with both thresholds stated so that patients know in advance what will not be reported.
policies.M054:c04: Let patients choose the categories and the timing of any secondary information, with the choices recorded, revisable, and honoured when a finding arises.
policies.M054:c05: Return actionable findings by default, on the ground that preventable morbidity justifies a weak default, with the default stated before sequencing and the opt-out genuinely available.
policies.M054:c06: Require explicit prior authorisation before return, on right-not-to-know grounds, with the authorisation specific to categories rather than given once for all findings.
policies.M054:c07: Use a staged recontact model that allows later choices rather than a one-time all-or-nothing consent, with the recontact route maintained and patients told how to use it.
policies.M055:c01: Leave disclosure to the consumer, supported by tools that help them tell relatives, with the tools provided by the service rather than left to the person to find.
policies.M055:c02: Provide structured service-mediated support for disclosure to relatives, with the service offering to make contact on the consumer's behalf and the consumer deciding whether it does.
policies.M055:c03: Operate a narrow pre-consented warning pathway for serious actionable familial risk, with consent to that pathway taken at registration and the conditions covered listed.
policies.M055:c04: Warn a relative without the consumer's consent only above a very high preventability and severity threshold, with the threshold stated in advance and each use reviewed independently.
policies.M055:c05: Protect confidentiality and consumer control, with any disclosure requiring the consumer's agreement and the service's obligations stated at registration.
policies.M055:c06: Recognise relatives' claim to actionable risk information on relational grounds, with the claim defined by what they could act on rather than by what they might want to know.
policies.M056:c01: Retain the fixed 14-day limit, with the boundary applied uniformly and any research requiring more days refused rather than reviewed case by case.
policies.M056:c02: Permit extension to a new fixed maximum under specialised review, with the new limit set publicly, the review body named, and its decisions recorded.
policies.M056:c03: Replace a universal day cutoff with staged developmental-milestone review of each project, with the milestones defined biologically and the review conducted before each stage.
policies.M056:c04: Permit extension only where scientific value is high and no adequate alternative exists, with both assessed by the review body and its reasoning published.
policies.M056:c05: Maintain a firm boundary on precautionary grounds about embryo moral status, with the boundary's function as a bright line stated as its justification rather than a biological claim.
policies.M056:c06: Permit controlled extension on proportionality grounds, with the research benefit stated concretely and the extension limited to what that benefit requires.
policies.M056:c07: Require periodic public or legislative reauthorisation rather than indefinite regulator discretion, with the interval fixed and the authorisation lapsing if not renewed.
policies.M057:c01: Require specialised review for all three-dimensional embryo-model work, with the reviewing body constituted for this purpose and its criteria published.
policies.M057:c02: Tier oversight by developmental capability, degree of integration, endpoint and scientific purpose, with the tiers defined in advance and the assignment of a project recorded.
policies.M057:c03: Prohibit reproductive transfer and high-integration experiments beyond defined limits, with the prohibited experiments listed specifically rather than described in general terms.
policies.M057:c04: Apply ordinary research oversight to low-capability models with escalation triggers, with the triggers defined as observable features and monitoring in place to detect them.
policies.M057:c05: Track moral concern to increasing organismal resemblance and capability, with the indicators named in advance so that escalation is automatic rather than discretionary.
policies.M057:c06: Oppose embryo-equivalent restrictions where embryo-equivalent capacities are absent, requiring any restriction to name the capacity it responds to rather than the resemblance.
policies.M057:c07: Publish what is being made, how far it develops and what happens to it, so that oversight is checkable from outside the specialist community, with reports at stated intervals.
policies.M058:c01: Permit broad clinical use under existing assisted-reproduction safeguards once safety is established, with the safety standard stated and the safeguards adapted to the new technique rather than assumed to transfer.
policies.M058:c02: Begin with restricted indications together with a registry and long-term follow-up, with participation mandatory, the indications listed, and expansion tied to registry findings.
policies.M058:c03: Permit no reproductive use until stronger evidence about offspring and about the social implications exists, naming the evidence sought so the restriction can end.
policies.M058:c04: Restrict initial use to infertility indications, with the indication defined clinically and any extension requiring a fresh public decision.
policies.M058:c05: Permit access irrespective of family form where the reproductive use is otherwise safe, with eligibility criteria stated so that family form cannot enter as an unwritten factor.
policies.M058:c06: Restrict uses that would enable non-consensual genetic parenthood or large-scale selection, with the prohibited uses defined and consent verified at the point of gamete derivation.
policies.M058:c07: Address access and intergenerational monitoring as a condition of permission, with the funding for both identified and the monitoring continuing beyond the first generation.
policies.M059:c01: Permit use for serious disease with case-by-case specialist approval and long-term follow-up, with the approval criteria published and follow-up mandatory and funded.
policies.M059:c02: Restrict to cases where alternatives offer little or no comparable benefit, with that comparison made for the specific family and recorded in the approval.
policies.M059:c03: Prohibit reproductive use pending longer-term safety evidence, naming the evidence and the studies that would produce it so the prohibition is reviewable.
policies.M059:c04: Favour availability for affected families under safeguards, with the safeguards specified and the families' own account of the burden of the condition recorded in the assessment.
policies.M059:c05: Require a registry and intergenerational monitoring on precautionary grounds, with participation a condition of treatment and the findings published as they accumulate.
policies.M059:c06: Favour access on reproductive-autonomy and beneficence grounds, with the decision left to the family once the safeguards are met and the uncertainties stated plainly.
policies.M059:c07: Restrict expansion beyond disease and require transparent oversight, with the boundary defined in advance and the oversight body's decisions published to maintain public trust.
policies.M060:c01: Permit informed non-medical sex selection, with counselling covering the reasons for the request and the clinic's policy published so that patients know before treatment.
policies.M060:c02: Decline all non-medical sex selection, with the policy stated publicly and applied uniformly rather than case by case.
policies.M060:c03: Permit selection only for family balancing, with the condition defined by the existing composition of the family and applied consistently rather than by the persuasiveness of the request.
policies.M060:c04: Permit each clinic a transparent policy of its own while requiring non-discriminatory disclosure before treatment begins, so that patients can choose a provider knowing its position.
policies.M060:c05: Favour permission on reproductive-liberty grounds, requiring any restriction to identify a harm beyond disapproval of the preference.
policies.M060:c06: Favour prohibition on gender-justice grounds, with the concern about reinforcing stereotypes stated and assessed for this population rather than in general.
policies.M060:c07: Permit only where coercion, sex-ratio and social-harm risks are low and counselling confirms the preference is the patient's own, with each assessed and recorded before treatment.
policies.M061:c01: Pay reasonable compensation for time, risk and inconvenience, alongside independent legal and medical safeguards, with the amount set in advance, independent counsel paid for by the programme, and medical decisions left to the carrier.
policies.M061:c02: Reimburse actual expenses only, with the categories listed, receipts not required for predictable costs, and payment made promptly rather than after the pregnancy ends.
policies.M061:c03: Pay structured compensation within a cap that recognises time and risk while limiting inducement, with the cap set against local income and published rather than negotiated per arrangement.
policies.M061:c04: Permit market-rate compensation subject to informed consent and to payment not being contingent on a healthy birth, with the non-contingency written into the contract and enforceable.
policies.M061:c05: Make the carrier the sole medical decision-maker throughout, regardless of the compensation agreed, with that term written into the contract and unwaivable.
policies.M061:c06: Require insurance, escrow, independent counsel and no outcome-contingent payment as conditions of any arrangement, with each verified before the transfer and audited by the programme.
policies.M061:c07: Set compensation so the carrier is never out of pocket and is paid for time and risk, with terms fixed in advance and independent legal advice paid for by the programme. Payment does not depend on the outcome, and the schedule is set out before any medical step begins.
policies.M062:c01: Permit the arrangement with enhanced independent counselling and consent, conducted separately with each party and covering how roles will be described to the child and to the wider family.
policies.M062:c02: Prohibit arrangements that would simulate consanguinity, with the prohibited relationships listed rather than assessed case by case.
policies.M062:c03: Require separate legal and psychological assessment where the arrangement is intergenerational or involves financial or caregiving dependency, with the assessment conducted independently of the recipients.
policies.M062:c04: Avoid intrafamilial arrangements broadly, on the ground that relational pressure is difficult to exclude, with exceptions requiring a documented finding that no such pressure exists.
policies.M062:c05: Permit where family support is genuinely voluntary and role clarity is protected, with both assessed independently and the intended roles recorded before treatment.
policies.M062:c06: Set stricter limits on anti-coercion grounds and to protect the child's family relationships, with the limits stated in policy and applied without exception for willing families.
policies.M062:c07: Give the donor a separate clinician and a private route to withdraw at any point, so that a family offer can be declined without the family learning why. The withdrawal is communicated by the clinic as a clinical outcome, and no reason is recorded that could be traced back.
policies.M063:c01: Prohibit reproductive cloning categorically, with the prohibition stated in law, applying to transfer rather than to technique, and enforced against providers.
policies.M063:c02: Reconsider only after safety is established and broad democratic authorisation obtained, with both required and neither sufficient alone, and the authorisation process specified.
policies.M063:c03: Permit if safety and identity concerns eventually become comparable to accepted assisted reproduction, with the comparison made explicitly and the evidence for it published.
policies.M063:c04: Prohibit on grounds of dignity and non-instrumentalisation, with the ground stated so that a later safety improvement does not by itself reopen the question.
policies.M063:c05: Permit limited research-only nuclear-transfer work without reproductive implantation, with the boundary enforced by licence conditions and the work reported.
policies.M063:c06: Consult broadly and publish the reasoning before any change of position, so that a prohibition is maintained or lifted by public decision rather than by the first laboratory to proceed. The consultation precedes any licensing decision and its outcome is published in full.
policies.M064:c01: Offer the technology as a rescue option after parental consent where the expected outcome exceeds conventional intensive care, with that expectation stated from the programme's own data rather than from projections.
policies.M064:c02: Restrict initially to trials and to specified gestational thresholds, with the thresholds stated, the trial registered, and outcomes published as they accumulate.
policies.M064:c03: Require use where it clearly offers materially better survival or neurodevelopment than standard care, with clearly and materially defined numerically rather than clinically judged.
policies.M064:c04: Let parents choose between conventional intensive care and the new technology where equipoise exists, with equipoise stated explicitly and both options described in equal detail.
policies.M064:c05: Restrict on precautionary grounds because long-term developmental effects are unknown, with the follow-up that would resolve this specified and funded.
policies.M064:c06: Prevent the technology from becoming available only at privileged centres or to privileged patients, with access monitored and reported by centre and by patient population.
policies.M064:c07: Keep the conventional neonatal option available in full, with the same staffing and follow-up, so that choosing it is not the lesser path. Its resourcing is protected explicitly rather than allowed to erode as the new pathway grows.
policies.M065:c01: Permit after alternatives have been exhausted and where the expected benefit to the sibling is substantial, with both established and recorded before treatment begins.
policies.M065:c02: Permit more broadly where the new child is independently wanted and donation is limited to cord blood or other low-burden tissue, with the limit written into the plan rather than left to later decision.
policies.M065:c03: Prohibit selection for instrumental donation, with the prohibition applying to the selection rather than to the family's reasons for wanting another child.
policies.M065:c04: Permit low-burden donation while requiring the donor child's own assent for anything invasive later, with the assent sought independently and a refusal respected.
policies.M065:c05: Limit the cumulative donation burden the future child may carry, with the limit stated in advance and counted across all donations rather than assessed one at a time.
policies.M065:c06: Favour access on parental reproductive-autonomy and rescue grounds, with the sibling's prognosis stated and the alternatives documented as exhausted.
policies.M065:c07: Require independent ethics review to confirm that no reasonable donor alternative exists and that the future child's interests are protected, with the review completed before treatment.
policies.M065:c08: Give the future donor child their own clinician and record now what they will be told, so that a child conceived to donate learns their history from the family rather than by accident. The record is made at conception and revisited as the child grows.
policies.M066:c01: Offer actionable fetal and parental secondary findings with an opt-out, with the categories listed before sequencing and the opt-out recorded per category.
policies.M066:c02: Report only findings relevant to fetal or childhood management, with the boundary stated in advance so that parents know what will not be reported.
policies.M066:c03: Allow opt-in to broader categories after counselling, with the counselling covering what each category could reveal about the parents as well as the fetus.
policies.M066:c04: Defer adult-onset fetal findings to protect the future child's own choice, with the finding retained and a recontact route explained to the parents.
policies.M066:c05: Return serious actionable parental findings separately and with their own consent, sought before sequencing rather than at the point of disclosure.
policies.M066:c06: Offer a category-based preference menu, with the categories described concretely and the choices recorded and revisable before results are issued.
policies.M066:c07: Report only what the diagnostic indication requires, unless an immediate preventable harm would otherwise be missed, with that exception stated in advance and applied narrowly.
policies.M067:c01: Offer established preservation routinely with the child's assent, with the offer made at diagnosis, the assent sought in the child's own terms, and a refusal recorded and respected.
policies.M067:c02: Permit parents to authorise low-burden tissue preservation where the child cannot assent, with the burden assessed and the child's later access to the decision recorded.
policies.M067:c03: Respect a postpubertal minor's objection, with the objection final for that procedure and the decision revisitable at the young person's own request.
policies.M067:c04: Defer invasive experimental preservation where the delay or burden would threaten cancer treatment, with the oncology team's assessment recorded and the option revisited if the schedule changes.
policies.M067:c05: Favour preserving reproductive options on future-autonomy grounds, with the future decision left to the child and the material stored accordingly.
policies.M067:c06: Limit experimental burden on present-welfare grounds, with the burden assessed against what the child is already undergoing rather than in isolation.
policies.M067:c07: Offer the counselling and the procedure without delaying cancer therapy, and record the child's own view whatever their age. Where the schedule cannot accommodate both, the therapy proceeds and the reason is recorded for the child to read later.
policies.M068:c01: Transfer the embryo for a manageable condition after counselling, with the condition's expected course described concretely and the counselling recorded.
policies.M068:c02: Decline transfer on child-welfare grounds, with the threshold stated in clinic policy in advance rather than applied to this patient's embryo alone.
policies.M068:c03: Transfer only where no unaffected embryo remains and severity falls below a defined harm threshold, with both conditions established and the threshold published.
policies.M068:c04: Favour patient choice on reproductive-liberty grounds, requiring any refusal to identify a harm to the future child rather than a preference about which lives should begin.
policies.M068:c05: Limit transfer above a severe-harm threshold on future-child welfare grounds, with the threshold defined by stated clinical criteria and applied consistently.
policies.M068:c06: Reject the assumption that a life with the condition is categorically not worth living, with any limit required to rest on the specific expected experience rather than on the diagnosis.
policies.M068:c07: Publish the clinic's transfer limits in advance and disclose them before treatment, with the policy given in writing at the first consultation.
policies.M068:c08: Tell patients the clinic's transfer policy before treatment begins, so that no one discovers a restriction after their embryos exist. The policy is given in writing at the first consultation and any change applies only to treatment started afterwards.
policies.M069:c01: Disclose the error or misdirection immediately, with what is known, what is not, and a commitment to updates on stated dates that happen whether or not there is news.
policies.M069:c02: Disclose the event promptly while staging uncertain causal details until they are verified, saying explicitly which details are being withheld and when they will be provided.
policies.M069:c03: Disclose even errors that caused no harm, on the ground that genetic and reproductive information matters in itself, with the disclosure made to the patient rather than logged internally.
policies.M069:c04: Do not disclose clearly harmless near misses unless a system-learning or patient-interest threshold is met, with the threshold defined in advance and near misses recorded internally regardless.
policies.M069:c05: Disclose fully on transparency and accountability grounds, with the disclosure covering what went wrong, why, and what has changed as a result.
policies.M069:c06: Provide a consolidated account once the facts are established, with an interim notification that an investigation is under way and a stated maximum period before the full account.
policies.M069:c07: Tell the affected patient every laboratory error touching their material as soon as it is known, including errors the clinic judges harmless, and say what remains uncertain. Each disclosure names who is investigating and when the patient will hear again.
policies.M070:c01: Prioritise by urgency and by impending loss of eligibility, with the eligibility windows stated and applied uniformly rather than to whoever is referred first.
policies.M070:c02: Prioritise by expected benefit and safety, with the estimates stated, the model published, and its distributional effects reported.
policies.M070:c03: Allocate by lottery within clinically comparable tiers, with the tiers defined in advance and the draw conducted outside the treating team.
policies.M070:c04: Combine prevalence, urgency, availability of a donor alternative and a lottery under a published rule, with the weight of each stated and the resulting allocations recorded.
policies.M070:c05: Give priority to historically underserved and high-burden communities to address structural inequity, with the criteria stated and the effect on access measured and published.
policies.M070:c06: Sequence by operational readiness subject to clinical minimums, with the minimums defined and readiness assessed on stated criteria rather than by centre relationships.
policies.M070:c07: Give more weight to patients with severe disease who accept higher treatment risk, with the risk explained in full and the preference recorded in the patient's own words.
policies.M071:c01: Compare against the established active treatment rather than placebo, accepting the larger sample this requires, with the comparator stated in the protocol and its adequacy assessed by the review committee.
policies.M071:c02: Use placebo only under the narrow exception for compelling methodological necessity, with that necessity argued in the protocol, assessed independently, and the exception cited explicitly.
policies.M071:c03: Use placebo with safeguards: the shortest washout consistent with the question, rescue treatment available immediately, and monitoring frequent enough to detect deterioration before harm.
policies.M071:c04: Permit methodologically necessary placebo where equipoise holds and social value is high, with both assessed by the review committee and the reasoning recorded rather than assumed from the design.
policies.M071:c05: Require an active control on non-maleficence grounds, on the ground that withholding effective treatment from a consenting participant is still a harm the trial imposes.
policies.M071:c06: Permit placebo only after unusually explicit consent and only where the professional risk threshold is still met, with the consent process documented and the threshold assessed independently of the participant's willingness.
policies.M071:c07: Guarantee that anyone assigned placebo returns to effective treatment immediately on worsening, and say plainly at consent how long they may be without it, with the rescue criteria written into the protocol.
policies.M072:c01: Approve under the full set of criteria for controlled human infection studies, with each criterion addressed in the protocol and the review body's assessment of each recorded.
policies.M072:c02: Require effective rescue treatment as a further condition of approval, with the treatment available on site, its efficacy established, and the plan for using it specified.
policies.M072:c03: Reject the study where residual risk or uncertainty exceeds a defined threshold, with the threshold stated in advance so that it constrains approval rather than describing it.
policies.M072:c04: Permit the study without curative treatment only where severity is low, rescue and supportive care are excellent, and social value is compelling, with all three established rather than argued in the aggregate.
policies.M072:c05: Permit the study on grounds of participant autonomy and high social value, with the value stated concretely — what the study would settle — rather than as a general appeal to importance.
policies.M072:c06: Restrict on precautionary non-maleficence grounds, with the uncertainty named and the restriction reviewable as the relevant evidence develops.
policies.M072:c07: Require enhanced compensation, care for any injury, and community engagement as conditions of approval, with each specified, funded and in place before recruitment.
policies.M072:c08: Fix compensation, treatment for any harm and long-term follow-up before recruitment opens, and publish those terms with the participant information, so that they are known rather than negotiated after an injury.
policies.M073:c01: Enrol under the exception from informed consent with the full regulatory and community safeguards, with community consultation and public disclosure completed and documented before enrolment begins.
policies.M073:c02: Enrol only with surrogate consent, and do not enrol where no surrogate is available, accepting the resulting limits on the evidence the trial can produce.
policies.M073:c03: Enrol immediately and seek authorisation from the patient or surrogate afterwards where the law permits, with the approach made as soon as practicable and withdrawal honoured including of data already collected.
policies.M073:c04: Waive consent only where there is a prospect of direct benefit and the intervention window makes consent infeasible, with both established in the protocol and reviewed independently.
policies.M073:c05: Keep the exception narrow on autonomy grounds, requiring that no lesser departure from consent would allow the question to be answered.
policies.M073:c06: Permit the exception to generate evidence for lethal emergencies that could not otherwise be researched, with the alternative — continuing to treat without evidence — stated explicitly in the justification.
policies.M073:c07: Consult the community the trial will enrol from before it begins and publish what was heard, so that people enrolled without consent were represented in the decision to allow it, with objections recorded rather than summarised.
policies.M074:c01: Use the global best-proven treatment as the control, with the sponsor supplying it for the trial's duration and the arrangement stated in the protocol.
policies.M074:c02: Use an enhanced local standard together with commitments on responsiveness and fair benefits, with the enhancement specified and the benefits agreed with the host before approval.
policies.M074:c03: Use the local standard only where scientifically necessary and where the avoidable harm stays within an ethical threshold, with both assessed independently and the threshold stated.
policies.M074:c04: Use the local standard on the ground that it reflects the context in which the treatment would be implemented, with that implementation claim made explicit and tested against the host's own plans.
policies.M074:c05: Require the sponsor to supply the better standard during the trial as a matter of justice, with the supply funded and its continuation after the trial addressed separately.
policies.M074:c06: Permit a contextual comparator where the trial materially strengthens future access, with the strengthening specified as commitments rather than expectations and reported afterwards.
policies.M074:c07: Reject the trial where the comparator would exploit unjust background conditions, with that judgment made by the review committee and the reasoning recorded.
policies.M074:c08: Commit in advance to what the host community gets if the treatment works, and publish that commitment with the protocol, in terms specific enough to be enforced.
policies.M075:c01: Take bounded broad consent for named research categories under published governance, with the categories described concretely and the governance body's decisions available to participants.
policies.M075:c02: Recontact for consent whenever a materially new category of use arises, with materiality defined in advance and the recontact route maintained rather than allowed to lapse.
policies.M075:c03: Take specific consent for each use, accepting the administrative burden, with the consent record linked to the sample so that use can be checked against it.
policies.M075:c04: Take broad consent with a working opt-out and withdrawal and a transparency portal showing what has actually been done, with the portal maintained and current rather than nominal.
policies.M075:c05: Use residual clinical samples under notice and opt-out where the law permits, with the notice given where patients will see it and the opt-out effective for future use.
policies.M075:c06: Favour granular control on autonomy grounds, with the choices offered in a form participants can revisit and change over time.
policies.M075:c07: Favour broad governed reuse on solidarity and social-value grounds, with the value produced reported back to participants rather than assumed.
policies.M076:c01: Pay fairly for time and burden without an arbitrary cap, with the rate published, the basis for it stated, and the same rate applied across studies of similar demand.
policies.M076:c02: Cap payment conservatively to reduce undue influence, with the cap justified against local income and its effect on who enrols monitored and reported.
policies.M076:c03: Permit high payment with enhanced consent and comprehension safeguards, with comprehension tested rather than assumed and the testing documented.
policies.M076:c04: Prorate payment so that it is earned as the study proceeds and withdrawal costs nothing already earned, with the schedule stated at consent and paid on withdrawal without delay.
policies.M076:c05: Pay market-like compensation on fairness grounds, treating participation as work that carries burden, with the rate set transparently and reviewed.
policies.M076:c06: Limit payment where it predictably distorts judgment for particular participants, with the limit targeted at the distortion rather than applied uniformly, and its basis stated.
policies.M076:c07: Pay for time and burden at a rate the participant can see and check, prorated so that leaving early costs nothing already earned, with the schedule given in writing before enrolment.
policies.M077:c01: Permit only minimal-risk procedures where there is no prospect of direct benefit, with minimal risk defined against the ordinary experiences of the children concerned and assessed by the committee.
policies.M077:c02: Permit a minor increase over minimal risk where social value and necessity are compelling, with parental permission and the child's assent, and each procedure classified explicitly in the protocol.
policies.M077:c03: Prohibit no-benefit procedures exceeding a minor increase over minimal risk regardless of assent, with the prohibition applying to the procedure rather than to the study as a whole.
policies.M077:c04: Permit broader participation where a mature adolescent's assent is strong and informed, with maturity assessed individually and the assent recorded in the young person's own words.
policies.M077:c05: Apply a child-protection standard, resolving uncertainty about risk against the study, with the reasoning recorded so that exclusion is a decision rather than a default.
policies.M077:c06: Permit carefully bounded burdens so that children are not excluded from the evidence that would improve their care, with the bounds stated and the resulting evidence gap named if the study is refused.
policies.M078:c01: Include pregnant participants presumptively with pregnancy-specific safeguards, with exclusion requiring a stated justification rather than inclusion requiring one.
policies.M078:c02: Include after adequate data in non-pregnant participants, with the threshold for adequate stated in advance and the inclusion step planned rather than left to a future decision.
policies.M078:c03: Exclude where fetal uncertainty or risk exceeds a stated threshold, with the threshold defined and the resulting evidence gap acknowledged in the protocol.
policies.M078:c04: Oppose routine exclusion on justice grounds, on the ground that the evidence gap is itself a harm, with that harm stated for the specific condition under study.
policies.M078:c05: Stage evidence generation on precautionary maternal-fetal grounds, with each stage's entry criteria defined and the timetable committed to rather than open-ended.
policies.M078:c06: Let a capable pregnant participant decide within independently acceptable risk limits, with those limits set by the committee and the decision left to the participant within them.
policies.M078:c07: Offer pregnant patients the trial rather than deciding for them, with the uncertainty stated plainly and their own clinician involved in the decision, and the offer recorded either way.
policies.M079:c01: Include research relevant to people in prison, with enhanced protections and prisoner representation on the review board, and the relevance established rather than asserted.
policies.M079:c02: Restrict non-therapeutic studies to minimal risk and to defined categories, with the categories stated in policy rather than judged for each protocol.
policies.M079:c03: Exclude people in prison from non-beneficial research categorically, accepting that the resulting evidence gap affects their care and stating it.
policies.M079:c04: Include where exclusion would itself create an evidence injustice and coercion safeguards are robust, with both established and the safeguards audited during the study.
policies.M079:c05: Apply heightened scrutiny rather than blanket exclusion, on the ground that vulnerability calls for protection rather than exclusion from benefit.
policies.M079:c06: Set strict benefit and relevance thresholds on anti-exploitation grounds, with the study required to address a condition or circumstance specific to imprisonment.
policies.M079:c07: Let people in prison decide without their participation affecting parole, privileges or housing, and say so in writing at consent, with the guarantee given by the institution rather than the researcher.
policies.M080:c01: Guarantee continued access to the intervention for as long as it is medically needed, with the commitment funded and stated in the protocol before enrolment.
policies.M080:c02: Fund a time-limited transition to health-system access, with the duration stated, the transition arranged rather than assumed, and participants told what happens at its end.
policies.M080:c03: Agree a fair-benefit plan before the trial with exceptions approved by the review committee, with the plan published and the exceptions recorded and justified.
policies.M080:c04: Provide no special entitlement beyond ordinary access once the study ends, stating this plainly at consent so that participants are not left expecting otherwise.
policies.M080:c05: Provide continued access on reciprocity and non-abandonment grounds, with the obligation running to the participants who bore the risk rather than to the population generally.
policies.M080:c06: Bound the duration of sponsor responsibility where an indefinite obligation would undermine future research or access equity, with the bound stated in advance and its rationale published.
policies.M081:c01: Post results to a public registry within a stated period for every completed human trial, and publish where appropriate, with compliance monitored rather than left to the sponsor.
policies.M081:c02: Publish a full manuscript for every scientifically interpretable trial, with the obligation written into the funding or sponsorship agreement and enforced.
policies.M081:c03: Allow limited discretion over manuscript detail while keeping public results mandatory, with the discretion bounded and the registry entry complete regardless.
policies.M081:c04: Require full dissemination on grounds of participants' contribution and social value, with the obligation stated to participants at enrolment.
policies.M081:c05: Permit concise public reporting where results are uninterpretable or redundant, while prohibiting suppression outright, with the judgment recorded and reviewable.
policies.M081:c06: Publish the result whatever it shows, within a stated period, and tell participants where to find it when they enrol, with a reminder sent when it appears.
policies.M082:c01: Obtain individual consent together with gatekeeper permission and community engagement, with the gatekeeper's role defined so it does not substitute for individual consent.
policies.M082:c02: Waive consent or use an opt-out for low-risk cluster interventions where individual consent is infeasible, with infeasibility established and the opt-out genuinely available to families.
policies.M082:c03: Obtain individual consent wherever feasible and permit no gatekeeper proxy consent, accepting the recruitment cost and stating it in the protocol.
policies.M082:c04: Give collective interests independent procedural weight through community authorisation, with the authorising body identified and its decision recorded before randomisation.
policies.M082:c05: Restrict waiver on individual-autonomy grounds, requiring that the intervention could not otherwise be studied and that each individual can still decline.
policies.M082:c06: Use community consultation with individual opt-out for population-level low-risk interventions, with both layers specified and the opt-out effective at the individual level.
policies.M082:c07: Consult the school communities before randomisation and publish what was decided, so that families whose children are covered by the change had a route to object before it applied.
policies.M083:c01: Offer confirmed clinically actionable findings, with the participant choosing at enrolment whether to receive them, confirmation in an accredited laboratory, and a route to clinical follow-up arranged rather than suggested.
policies.M083:c02: Offer a broader set of valid findings according to categories the participant selects, with the categories described concretely at enrolment and the selection revisable.
policies.M083:c03: Return only findings meeting a stated validity and actionability threshold, with the threshold published so that participants know in advance what they will and will not hear.
policies.M083:c04: Return urgent actionable findings even where the participant made no prior request, where serious preventable harm is at stake, with that exception stated at enrolment rather than applied unannounced.
policies.M083:c05: Honour a right not to know through an opt-out recorded at enrolment, applied to all categories the participant declines, and revisited only if the participant asks.
policies.M083:c06: Return more broadly on grounds of participants' access to their own data, with interpretation support provided so that returning a result is not merely transferring a burden.
policies.M083:c07: Do not return uncertain or unvalidated findings, while keeping a recontact route open should the finding later be reclassified, with the route maintained and participants told it exists.
policies.M084:c01: Preserve investigator publication freedom, subject to a short sponsor review confined to confidential or intellectual-property material, with the review period fixed and no veto over content.
policies.M084:c02: Permit a fixed limited delay for patent filing or multi-site coordination, with the maximum stated in the contract and no extension available by negotiation.
policies.M084:c03: Publish immediately except for narrowly defined confidential information, with that category listed in the contract rather than identified at the time of submission.
policies.M084:c04: Allow the sponsor to coordinate first publication within a hard deadline while holding no veto, with the deadline stated and publication proceeding automatically once it passes.
policies.M084:c05: Weigh scientific independence against legitimate intellectual-property reliance, and state in the agreement which consideration governs where they conflict.
policies.M084:c06: Publish the contract terms governing publication alongside the trial registration, so that participants can see what the sponsor may withhold before enrolling, with the terms summarised in the participant information.
policies.M085:c01: Proceed in adults with severe disease and no alternative, under enhanced oversight and staged dosing, with the oversight body independent and the staging rules fixed before the first participant.
policies.M085:c02: Require a stronger preclinical threshold before first human exposure, with the threshold specified in terms of the studies to be completed and their results, rather than in general terms.
policies.M085:c03: Restrict initial enrolment to the group with the highest need and the fewest alternatives, with eligibility defined clinically and applied consistently rather than by referral order.
policies.M085:c04: Use sentinel dosing and escalation with stopping rules fixed in advance, with a mandatory observation interval between participants and escalation requiring independent sign-off.
policies.M085:c05: Permit carefully managed uncertainty for otherwise untreatable disease, with the management specified — monitoring, stopping, rescue — rather than asserted as careful.
policies.M085:c06: Delay human exposure on precautionary grounds, naming what would have to be established first so that the delay has an end condition rather than deferring indefinitely.
policies.M085:c07: Prevent desperation from standing in for consent quality and guarantee long-term follow-up coverage, with comprehension assessed independently and follow-up funded before enrolment.
policies.M085:c08: Say plainly at consent that this is a first-in-human study and cannot be expected to treat the participant's own disease, and give the same care afterwards to those it does not help, with that care funded and arranged.
policies.M086:c01: Direct supply to the trial to generate reliable evidence, with the reasoning published and the expected date by which the evidence would be available stated.
policies.M086:c02: Reserve a stated fraction for expanded access to the worst-off patients ineligible for the trial, with the fraction fixed in advance and the eligibility criteria published.
policies.M086:c03: Supply the trial first and permit expanded access only from surplus that does not interfere, with interference defined in terms of recruitment and timelines rather than judged case by case.
policies.M086:c04: Allocate expanded access by lottery among eligible patients, with the eligibility criteria and the draw both public and the draw run outside the treating team.
policies.M086:c05: Prioritise within expanded access by urgency and worst-off status, with the criteria stated in advance and each allocation recorded against them.
policies.M086:c06: Give priority to evidence generation on social-value grounds, stating what the trial would establish and for how many future patients.
policies.M086:c07: Give priority to patients excluded from the trial through no fault of their own, with exclusion reasons recorded and the compassion route defined rather than ad hoc.
policies.M086:c08: Publish the allocation rule and the numbers available, so that patients who receive nothing can see how the decision was made rather than suspecting it, with the numbers updated as supply changes.
policies.M087:c01: Permit a sham control only where it is scientifically necessary and the incremental risk over the trial's other procedures is low, with both established in the protocol and assessed independently.
policies.M087:c02: Require an active or usual-care control wherever sham risk exceeds a stated threshold, with the threshold defined by procedure rather than judged per study.
policies.M087:c03: Permit sham with enhanced consent, rescue provision and risk mitigation where equipoise holds, with each element specified and the equipoise judgment recorded.
policies.M087:c04: Permit low-risk sham after transparent consent on autonomy grounds, with the consent describing the sham procedure concretely rather than as a control condition.
policies.M087:c05: Reject non-therapeutic invasive procedures where a less risky design could answer the question, with the alternative design considered explicitly and its rejection justified.
policies.M087:c06: Permit sham where placebo and procedural effects would otherwise make blinded causal inference unreliable, with that methodological claim argued and reviewed rather than assumed.
policies.M087:c07: Tell participants exactly what the sham involves and its risks, and guarantee the real procedure afterwards if the trial shows it works, with that guarantee funded and stated at consent.
policies.M088:c01: Run an adaptive platform with independent oversight and every adaptation rule prespecified, with the oversight body seeing unblinded data and the rules registered before the first participant.
policies.M088:c02: Run separate fixed trials, accepting slower learning in exchange for simpler inference and clearer accountability at each site.
policies.M088:c03: Use an adaptive design only where the emergency learning advantage justifies the added complexity, with that advantage stated in the protocol and assessed by the review committee.
policies.M088:c04: Use response-adaptive allocation toward better-performing arms, subject to inferential safeguards specified in advance, with the allocation rule registered and the safeguards independently reviewed.
policies.M088:c05: Favour platform efficiency on social-value grounds, with the expected gain in time-to-answer stated rather than assumed from the design.
policies.M088:c06: Favour simpler fixed designs where adaptation would impair comprehensibility or local accountability, with that judgment made against the actual sites and populations involved.
policies.M088:c07: Publish the adaptation rules before the trial starts and explain to each participant how their allocation may change, so that a moving design remains something they consented to. The rules are registered with the protocol, the explanation is given in the information sheet rather than on request, and any change to the rules is published before it takes effect.
policies.M089:c01: Allocate to maximise expected population health gain against disease burden, with the burden measure and the modelling published and revisited each cycle.
policies.M089:c02: Prioritise neglected conditions and worst-off populations, with neglect and disadvantage measured on stated indicators and the resulting portfolio published.
policies.M089:c03: Build the portfolio through a participatory multiprinciple process, with the principles, the participants and the resulting weights all published.
policies.M089:c04: Reserve a stated fraction for high-risk transformative research, ring-fenced from the main allocation and assessed on different criteria, both published.
policies.M089:c05: Prioritise near-term implementation and scalability, with those criteria defined and the trade-off against longer-term discovery stated rather than left implicit.
policies.M089:c06: Allocate proportionally to disease burden with explicit equity weights, publishing the weights so that the departure from pure proportionality is visible.
policies.M089:c07: Set the agenda through public deliberation with periodic re-evaluation, with the deliberation's composition and conclusions published and the re-evaluation on a fixed schedule.
policies.M089:c08: Give patients and the public a standing role in setting the portfolio, with the reasoning for the final split published, and the role continuing between cycles rather than convened for each.
policies.M090:c01: Layer individual consent with Tribal or community governance for secondary use, with both required and neither treated as sufficient alone, and the governance route named in the agreement.
policies.M090:c02: Require community approval for specified uses alongside individual consent where individual consent applies, with the specified uses listed and any addition requiring fresh approval.
policies.M090:c03: Require a new agreement and review for materially new secondary research, with materiality defined by the community rather than by the researcher.
policies.M090:c04: Rely on individual consent alone, stating that position explicitly so that communities know what governance the study does and does not recognise.
policies.M090:c05: Apply a collective-benefit and data-sovereignty standard, with the community controlling access, storage and future use, and the arrangement documented in a binding agreement.
policies.M090:c06: Maintain an individual-consent floor so that community authorisation cannot substitute for personal consent where person-level consent is ethically required, with that floor stated in the agreement.
policies.M091:c01: Require the lower-carbon design wherever validity and participant safety are preserved, with the comparison documented in the protocol and reviewed by the committee.
policies.M091:c02: Apply a proportional sustainability requirement based on avoidable emissions and the cost of avoiding them, with the threshold stated and applied consistently across protocols.
policies.M091:c03: Put scientific and participant priorities first with voluntary mitigation, stating what mitigation was considered and why it was or was not adopted.
policies.M091:c04: Treat avoidable research emissions as health externalities that the trial imposes, with them estimated and reported alongside the trial's other burdens.
policies.M091:c05: Avoid low-emission designs that shift burden to participants or sites in lower-resource settings, with the distribution of burden assessed explicitly before the design is fixed.
policies.M091:c06: Require lifecycle reporting and carbon accountability even where a lower-emission redesign is infeasible, with the reporting published alongside the results.
policies.M091:c07: Choose the design that reduces participant travel and time, and say what the trial asks of participants before asking them to join, with visit numbers and durations stated in the information sheet.
policies.M092:c01: Proceed with layered biorisk assessment, mitigation and oversight, with each layer specified, the residual risk stated, and the oversight continuing through the work rather than ending at approval.
policies.M092:c02: Modify aims, methods or information handling to reduce risk while preserving value, with the modifications recorded and the residual risk reassessed after them.
policies.M092:c03: Do not conduct the work above a defined unacceptable-risk threshold, with the threshold stated in institutional policy rather than set for this proposal.
policies.M092:c04: Require independent specialised review before initiation and again before continuation, with the reviewers' expertise specified and their decisions recorded.
policies.M092:c05: Favour managed research on grounds of scientific freedom and social value, with the value stated concretely and the management specified rather than promised.
policies.M092:c06: Favour non-performance where low-probability catastrophic harm dominates the assessment, with that dominance argued explicitly rather than asserted.
policies.M092:c07: Publish what oversight was applied and by whom, so that the public can see a decision was taken rather than assumed, including for work that was approved without modification.
policies.M093:c01: Publish in full where misuse risk is low, with that assessment made by an independent reviewer and recorded rather than left to the authors.
policies.M093:c02: Publish the conclusions and results while redacting high-risk enabling detail or placing it behind controlled access, with the access route functional and the redaction noted in the paper.
policies.M093:c03: Decline dissemination above an unacceptable misuse threshold, with the threshold defined in advance and the decision made by a body other than the funder.
policies.M093:c04: Require independent security and ethics review before any restrictive publication decision, with the review's reasoning recorded and available to the authors.
policies.M093:c05: Favour maximal disclosure on open-science and reproducibility grounds, with any restriction required to show what specific harm it prevents.
policies.M093:c06: Favour tiered access where the marginal scientific value of open detail is low relative to misuse risk, with both sides of that comparison stated.
policies.M093:c07: Say publicly that information has been withheld and on what grounds, so that restriction is visible and can be challenged, with a route for other researchers to request access.
policies.M094:c01: Mandate vaccination with medical exemptions once a necessity and proportionality threshold is met, with the threshold stated in advance, the mandate time-limited, and its continuation reviewed as transmission changes.
policies.M094:c02: Mandate only after voluntary and access measures have been tried and shown insufficient, with what was tried and what it achieved published before the mandate takes effect.
policies.M094:c03: Remain voluntary while investing intensively in access and education — free vaccination, paid time off, outreach to under-served groups — with uptake reported and the strategy adjusted rather than abandoned.
policies.M094:c04: Require vaccination or an alternative — testing, masking, reassignment — wherever an alternative is workable, with the alternatives specified and available in practice rather than nominally.
policies.M094:c05: Mandate on collective harm-prevention grounds, with the harm quantified for this outbreak and the mandate ending when that harm falls below the stated threshold.
policies.M094:c06: Keep measures voluntary on liberty and trust grounds unless an extreme threshold is crossed, with the threshold defined in advance so that it constrains the decision rather than describing it afterwards.
policies.M094:c07: Before any coercive policy, guarantee free vaccination, paid time to attend and recover, support for adverse events, and exemptions applied without discrimination, with each in place and reported rather than promised.
policies.M095:c01: Support voluntary isolation first — accommodation, income, food, medical care — with compulsion available only as a backstop, and the support delivered before compulsion is considered rather than alongside it.
policies.M095:c02: Isolate compulsorily at once where transmission risk is high and imminent and delay would materially endanger others, with both conditions recorded at the time and reviewed within a stated period.
policies.M095:c03: Use coercion only after less restrictive alternatives have failed, with those alternatives named, offered, and their failure documented before any order is made.
policies.M095:c04: Impose compulsory isolation for a fixed period with due process, independent review and material support, with the period stated in the order and extension requiring fresh findings.
policies.M095:c05: Apply a very high necessity threshold on liberty grounds, requiring that no lesser measure could achieve the objective and that the finding be reviewable by someone independent.
policies.M095:c06: Permit restriction only where housing, income and medical support are provided, on reciprocity grounds, with the supports arranged before the restriction begins rather than promised during it.
policies.M095:c07: Provide income, housing, food and contact with family for the whole period, so that isolation does not cost a person their livelihood or their household, with each arranged before the period starts.
policies.M096:c01: Add the condition to the universal panel once evidence and governance thresholds are met, with both stated in advance, the decision published, and the panel reviewed as evidence accumulates.
policies.M096:c02: Pilot with structured data collection before universal expansion, with the outcomes to be measured, the duration, and the decision rule for expanding all fixed at the start.
policies.M096:c03: Defer until the evidence for early intervention is stronger, naming what evidence is sought and what study would produce it, so that deferral has an end rather than becoming permanent.
policies.M096:c04: Add the condition with parental opt-out rather than as a mandatory screen, with the opt-out explained before the sample is taken and recorded without affecting other screening.
policies.M096:c05: Favour early detection under uncertainty on child-benefit grounds, accepting some false positives, with the follow-up pathway funded and in place before screening begins.
policies.M096:c06: Resist universal adoption until net benefit is clearer, on precautionary and overdiagnosis grounds, with the expected number of harmless findings stated rather than left implicit.
policies.M096:c07: Give parents a plain account of what a positive result would and would not mean, including the chance of finding something that never causes harm, before the sample is taken and in writing.
policies.M097:c01: Establish the service as harm reduction, with its objectives — overdose deaths, injecting-related infection, referrals — stated in advance and reported publicly against baseline.
policies.M097:c02: Do not establish the service and invest instead in treatment and prevention, with the alternative investment specified, funded, and its outcomes reported on the same terms.
policies.M097:c03: Run a time-limited evaluated pilot with outcomes defined before it opens and a decision rule for continuing, expanding or closing that is published at the outset.
policies.M097:c04: Integrate the service with naloxone distribution, treatment referral, wound care and housing and social support, so that a visit connects to those services rather than ending at the door.
policies.M097:c05: Put neighbourhood safeguards and continuing community engagement in place — siting, hours, waste management, a route for complaints — with the arrangements published and reviewed with residents.
policies.M097:c06: Favour the service on autonomy and harm-reduction grounds, treating people who use drugs as entitled to health care on the same terms as anyone else, with that stated in the service's terms.
policies.M097:c07: Prefer alternative interventions on grounds of normalisation, resource displacement and local externalities, with each concern stated specifically and tested against evidence rather than asserted.
policies.M097:c08: Involve residents and people who use drugs in siting and operating the service, and publish what was agreed, so that the arrangement is one the neighbourhood recognises and can hold the service to.
policies.M098:c01: Allocate to maximise near-term survival, using a stated prognostic measure applied identically to every patient, with the measure published and reassessed as the surge evolves.
policies.M098:c02: Combine expected benefit with an equity rule under a published multiprinciple standard, with the weight given to each stated and the resulting allocations audited.
policies.M098:c03: Allocate by lottery among clinically indistinguishable patients, with indistinguishability defined by stated criteria and the draw conducted and recorded by someone outside the treating team.
policies.M098:c04: Give priority by urgency and to the worst-off within a clinically meaningful band, with the band defined so that priority does not extend to patients who cannot benefit.
policies.M098:c05: Use a weighted lottery once a minimum clinical threshold is met, with the weights published in advance and the draw independently run.
policies.M098:c06: Allocate first-come first-served among eligible patients, with eligibility defined clinically and the ordering recorded so that it can be checked afterwards.
policies.M098:c07: Exclude social worth and long-term disability from the criteria and audit the rule for structural bias in how it operates, with the audit published and the rule amended where bias is found.
policies.M098:c08: Publish the triage rule before it is needed and tell patients and families when it is in force, so that no one learns the rule from the decision about them. The rule is displayed where patients arrive, its activation is announced publicly, and any change to it during the surge is published before it is applied.
policies.M099:c01: Apply the ordinary cost-effectiveness threshold, with the calculation and its assumptions published so that a refusal can be examined rather than only received.
policies.M099:c02: Apply a higher threshold weighted for severity and rarity, with the weighting fixed in advance and applied to every comparable condition rather than to this one.
policies.M099:c03: Cover conditionally while evidence is developed, with the data to be collected, the review date and the consequence of failing to meet the endpoints written into the agreement.
policies.M099:c04: Negotiate price, a budget cap or outcomes-based access, with the terms published in enough detail that the effective price and what happens when outcomes fall short are both visible.
policies.M099:c05: Favour substantial access for rare severe conditions on equal-rights grounds despite the opportunity cost, stating what that cost is rather than leaving it unquantified.
policies.M099:c06: Favour the interventions generating the most aggregate health, applying the rule consistently and reporting what the refused therapy would have delivered for the patients concerned.
policies.M099:c07: Give extra weight to very severe disease independent of rarity, with severity measured on a stated scale so that rarity does not enter the decision under another name.
policies.M099:c08: Involve patients with the condition in the coverage decision and publish the reasoning, including what was given up, so that a refusal can be understood and contested. The involvement happens before the decision is drafted, and the published reasoning names the alternative uses of the money and the route to appeal.
policies.M100:c01: Prioritise expected near-term benefit, assessed on stated clinical criteria applied to every candidate at the same time, with the comparison recorded.
policies.M100:c02: Give priority by urgency and to the worst-off, with the assessment made across all candidates together rather than as each is referred, and recorded for review.
policies.M100:c03: Admit for a time-limited trial where prognosis is uncertain, with the review point and the criteria for continuing agreed at admission and applied when they fall due.
policies.M100:c04: Allocate by lottery among similarly eligible patients, with eligibility defined clinically, the draw run outside the treating team, and the outcome recorded.
policies.M100:c05: Use a published score combining urgency, expected benefit, expected duration of need and fair process, applied by someone not treating the patients being compared.
policies.M100:c06: Admit first-come first-served among clinically eligible patients, with eligibility assessed in advance and the queue recorded so that the ordering can be checked.
policies.M100:c07: Hold capacity in reserve for predictable emergencies rather than filling every bed from the current queue, with the reserve level set in advance and reviewed against actual demand.
policies.M100:c08: Tell the patients and families not admitted that a bed was unavailable and what will happen instead, rather than presenting the decision as purely clinical, and record what was said.
policies.M101:c01: Use age as a limited tie-break in favour of the younger candidate only where the medical criteria leave the candidates equivalent, with the size of the tie-break fixed in the allocation rule and published.
policies.M101:c02: Give age no independent weight, allowing it to enter only through the clinical variables it predicts, with the allocation rule stating that age itself is not a criterion.
policies.M101:c03: Use age-related information only to the extent it improves the prognostic estimate, with the prognostic model published and audited for whether age is doing work beyond prediction.
policies.M101:c04: Allocate by neutral lottery where candidates are otherwise equivalent, with equivalence defined by stated criteria and the draw conducted outside the transplant team.
policies.M101:c05: Give priority on fair-innings grounds to the candidate who has had less life, with the principle stated openly in the allocation rule rather than embedded in a prognostic proxy.
policies.M101:c06: Reject age as an index of moral worth, requiring any use of it to be justified as prediction and audited for whether it functions as a judgment about whose life matters.
policies.M102:c01: Let the deceased person's explicit or deemed consent prevail, with the family informed rather than asked, and the basis of the consent — registration or deemed — recorded and shown to them.
policies.M102:c02: Allow the family to veto despite deemed consent, with the veto recorded and the deceased's registration status noted so that the effect of the policy on registered donors is visible.
policies.M102:c03: Consult the family with a rebuttable presumption in favour of donation, with what would rebut it defined in advance rather than settled by the strength of the objection.
policies.M102:c04: Allow a veto only where there is credible evidence that the deceased objected, with the evidence recorded and assessed by someone other than the requesting clinician.
policies.M102:c05: Run a time-limited conflict and support process before recovery, with the period stated, bereavement support provided throughout, and the outcome recorded either way.
policies.M102:c06: Treat the donor's own decision as controlling on autonomy grounds, with the register's status explained publicly so that people know what registering will and will not achieve.
policies.M102:c07: Give the family a stronger role where the deceased's wishes are unknown, on relational grounds, with the distinction between unknown and known-and-contrary applied consistently and recorded.
policies.M103:c01: Set a programme-level upper risk ceiling that applies despite the donor's willingness, with the ceiling stated numerically, published, and applied by the programme rather than by the individual surgeon.
policies.M103:c02: Assess risk and benefit individually with an independent donor advocate involved throughout, with the advocate reporting separately and having authority to pause the process.
policies.M103:c03: Permit unusually high risk where a competent donor persistently accepts it and no coercion is found, with persistence assessed over a stated period and the coercion screening conducted privately.
policies.M103:c04: Prohibit donation beyond a threshold on the ground that clinicians may not intentionally expose a healthy person to disproportionate harm, with the threshold institutional and the reasoning explained to the donor.
policies.M103:c05: Count the donor's psychosocial benefit in the assessment without treating it as unlimited, with the weight it may carry bounded in advance so that willingness cannot offset any level of risk.
policies.M103:c06: Require enhanced independent review for exceptional-risk donation, conducted by people outside the transplant programme, with their finding recorded and binding.
policies.M103:c07: Give the donor an independent advocate, a private route to withdraw, and a plain account of the risk in their own terms, at every stage rather than only at consent, with the withdrawal route usable without the recipient knowing.
policies.M104:c01: Assess future clinical benefit and expected adherence as for any candidate, with no penalty for the earlier record beyond what it predicts, and with the prediction stated and reviewable.
policies.M104:c02: Require that the barriers be mitigated and current ability to adhere evidenced before relisting, with the barriers named, the support in place, and the evidence period stated in advance.
policies.M104:c03: Lower priority only where a clinically meaningful and modifiable recurrence risk remains, with the risk quantified and the modification attempted before priority is reduced.
policies.M104:c04: Reject desert-based penalties on equal-opportunity grounds, requiring any weighting to be justified by prediction and audited for whether it is operating as punishment.
policies.M104:c05: Permit weighting for clinically relevant recurrence risk on stewardship grounds, with the weighting published and applied identically to all causes of graft loss.
policies.M104:c06: Use a restorative time-limited eligibility plan with support milestones rather than permanent exclusion, with the milestones agreed with the patient and relisting automatic on meeting them.
